$$ \left|\varepsilon_{\omega}\left(\widehat{H}_{F_{\omega}}(\tilde{x}_{\omega})-\frac{1}{d^{k}}\log|F^{(k)}(\tilde{x}_{\omega})|_{\omega}\right)\right|\leq\frac{C}{d^{k}} $$

for all $\omega\in\beta\mathbb{N}$ . Finally, by direct computation it is clear that

$$ \lim_{\omega}\frac{\varepsilon_{n}}{d^{k}}\log|F_{n}^{(k)}(\tilde{x}_{n})|_{n}=\varepsilon_{\omega}\log|F_{\omega}^{(k)}(\tilde{x}_{\omega})|_{\omega}, $$

as $(F_{n}^{(k)})$ is a sequence of polynomials whose coefficients gives $F_{\omega}^{(k)}$ . We thus obtain

$$ \left|(\lim_{\omega}\varepsilon_{n}\widehat{H}_{F_{n}}(\tilde{x}_{n})-\widehat{H}_{F_{\omega}}(\tilde{x}_{\omega})\right|\leq\frac{C}{d^{k}}. $$

Taking $k\to\infty$ yields

$$ \lim_{\omega}\varepsilon_{n}\widehat{H}_{F_{n}}(\tilde{x}_{n})=\widehat{H}_{F_{\omega}}(\tilde{x}_{\omega}) $$

as desired.∎

Now let $A$ be a ppav defined over an algebraically closed complete non-archimedean valued field $K$ , and assume its corresponding $K$ -point of $X$ lies in $U$ . Let $L$ be as in (26).

By properness, we obtain an $R$ -point of $\overline{\cal{A}}_{g,p}$ and hence a semiabelian scheme $\cal{G}$ lifting $A$ . Fix any increasing function $h:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ such that $h(n)=c(k_{n})$ for some $k_{n}$ . If $A$ has bad reduction, we say that $A$ is $n$ -good if for any collection of $x_{1},\ldots,x_{h(n)}$ many points which all lift to $R$ -points of $\cal{G}$ , we have

$$ g_{\cal{B}_{k_{n}}}(x_{1},\ldots,x_{c(k_{n})})\geq\frac{1}{n}\lambda_{\partial X}(A)+r(F_{K}) $$

where $X=\cal{A}_{g,3}$ and $\cal{B}_{k_{n}}$ is any good basis of $H^{0}(A,L^{k_{n}})$ . Fix a constant $C>0$ . Recall that we have fixed an affine open $U\subset X=\cal{A}_{g,3}$ at the start of the section. We say that our abelian $A/K$ whose induced $K$ -point on $\cal{A}_{g,3}$ lies in $U(K)$ is $C$ -centered with respect to our affine open $U$ if

$$ \lambda_{\partial U}(A)\leq C\lambda_{\partial X}(A). $$

Here, we define $\lambda_{\partial U}$ using the minimal compactification $\cal{A}_{g,3}^{*}$ of $\cal{A}_{g,3}$ . The main theorem of this section is then the following.

#### Theorem 5.2.

For any increasing function $h:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ where for each $n$ , we have $h(n)=c(k)$ for some $k\in\mathbb{N}$ , and any $C>0$ , there exists a nonempty finite list of integers $\{n_{1},\ldots,n_{m}\}$ such that for any non-archimedean complete algebraically closed field $K$ with $\mathbb{C}$ a trivially valued subfield, and for any principally polarized abelian variety $A/K$ of dimension $g$ with bad reduction which is $C$ -centered with respect to $U$ , we have that

$$ A/K\text{ is }n_{i}\text{-good for some }i\text{ with }1\leq i\leq m. $$

The set $\{n_{1},\ldots,n_{m}\}$ can depend on the open set $U$ along with the rational map $f$ and homogeneous lift $F$ . However, it is independent of $K$ and the dimension $g$ principally polarized abelian variety $A/K$ which is $C$ -centered with respect to $U$ .

#### Proof.

Assume no such nonempty finite set $\{n_{1},\ldots,n_{m}\}$ exists. Then we can find a sequence of dimension $g$ ppavs $A_{n}$ over $K_{n}$ having bad reduction, each $C$ -centered with respect to $U$ , such that for all $1\leq i\leq n$ , the abelian variety $A_{n}$ is not $i$ -good for all $1\leq i\leq n$ . We fix choices of principal level $3$ structures so that each $A_{n}$ defines a point on $X=\cal{A}_{g,3}$ . For each $n$ , let $L_{n}$ be the line bundle on $A_{n}$ as in (26). By assumption, after fixing a positive integer $n$ , for all $n^{\prime}\geq n$ , if $h(n)=c(k)$ , then there exists a good basis $\cal{B}^{\prime}_{n^{\prime}}$ of $H^{0}(A_{n^{\prime}},L_{n^{\prime}}^{k})$ , along with points $x_{n^{\prime},1},\ldots,x_{n^{\prime},c(k)}$ of $A_{n^{\prime}}(K_{n^{\prime}})$ that lift to $R_{n^{\prime}}$ -points of the semiabelian model $G_{n^{\prime}}$ of $A_{n^{\prime}}$ , such that

$$ g_{\cal{B}^{\prime}_{n^{\prime}}}(x_{n^{\prime},1},\ldots,x_{n^{\prime},c(k)})\leq\frac{1}{n}\lambda_{\partial X}(A_{n^{\prime}})+r(F_{n^{\prime}}). $$

Now recall that any good basis $\cal{B}^{\prime}_{n^{\prime}}$ is a finite subset of $\cal{F}\subseteq H^{0}(\mathbb{P}^{N}_{U},\cal{O}(k))$ where $\cal{F}$ is defined in (25). We now pass to a subsequence of $A_{n}$ ’s so that each good basis $\cal{B}^{\prime}_{n^{\prime}}$ of $H^{0}(A_{n^{\prime}},L^{k}_{n^{\prime}})$ is induced from the same set of sections of $H^{0}(\mathbb{P}_{U}^{N},\cal{O}(k))$ . We may do this as there are only finitely many possible subsets of $\cal{F}$ .

Let $\varepsilon_{n}=\lambda_{\partial X}(A_{n})^{-1}$ , which is finite because of Proposition 4.4. Then by Proposition 4.3, an $(\varepsilon_{n})$ -degeneration of $(A_{n})$ exists on $\cal{A}_{g,3}$ . Furthermore since each $A_{n}$ is $C$ -centered, it follows that our $(\varepsilon_{n})$ -degeneration actually exists on $U$ . Thus we obtain an abelian scheme $A_{\mathscr{A}^{\varepsilon}}$ over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathscr{A}^{\varepsilon}$ with an embedding $A_{\mathscr{A}^{\varepsilon}}\xrightarrow{}\mathbb{P}^{N}_{\mathscr{A}^{\varepsilon}}$ and an extension $f:\mathbb{P}^{N}\to\mathbb{P}^{N}$ of multiplication by $[n]$ on $A_{\mathscr{A}^{\varepsilon}}$ along with a homogeneous lift $F$ of $f$ .

Choose a non-principal ultrafilter $\omega$ . By Proposition 4.5, $A_{\omega}$ has bad reduction over $\cal{H}(\omega)$ , so there is a continuous map $r:A_{\omega}^{\operatorname{an}}\to\mathbb{R}^{k}/\Lambda$ where $\Lambda$ is a lattice and $k\geq 1$ . Let $V$ be the closed set that retracts to the identity $0$ of $S(A_{\omega})$ .

Let $L_{\omega}$ be the line bundle on $A_{\omega}^{\operatorname{an}}$ as in (26) for $\cal{H}(\omega)$ . Then by Proposition 3.2, we know that for any sequence of good bases $(\cal{B}_{k})$ of $H^{0}(A_{\omega},L_{\omega}^{k})$ , there exists a $\delta>0$ such that we have

$$ \liminf_{k\to\infty}\inf_{(x_{i})}g_{\cal{B}_{k}}(x_{1},\ldots,x_{c(k)})>\delta+r(F_{\omega}) $$

where we take the infimum over all $c(k)$ -tuples of classical points $(x_{i})$ such that $x_{i}\in V\cap A_{\omega}(\cal{H}(\omega))$ . Pick an $m\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0}$ large enough so that $\delta\geq\frac{1}{m}$ and

$$ \inf_{(x_{i})}g_{\cal{B}_{k}}(x_{1},\ldots,x_{c(k)})>\delta+r(F_{\omega}) $$

where $c(k)=h(m)$ and $\cal{B}_{k}$ is any good basis of $H^{0}(A_{\omega},L_{\omega}^{k})$ .

We now consider $m^{\prime}\geq m$ and let $h(m)=c(k)$ . We set $\cal{B}^{\prime}_{\omega}$ to be the subset of $H^{0}(A_{\omega},L_{\omega}^{k})$ that is induced from the same set of sections of $H^{0}(\mathbb{P}^{N}_{U},\cal{O}(k))$ as our good bases $\cal{B}^{\prime}_{n^{\prime}}$ . We now apply Proposition 5.1 and obtain

$$ g_{\cal{B}^{\prime}_{\omega}}(x_{1},\ldots,x_{c(k)})\leq\lim_{\omega}\left(\frac{1}{m}\lambda_{\partial X}(A_{m^{\prime}})\varepsilon_{m^{\prime}}+r(F_{m^{\prime}})\varepsilon_{m^{\prime}}\right)=\frac{1}{m}+r(F_{\omega}), $$

where we take the $\omega$ -limit over the $m^{\prime}$ and each $x_{i}$ is the $\omega$ -limit of the sequence $(x_{m^{\prime},i},x_{m^{\prime}+1,i},\ldots)$ . Note that $\cal{B}^{\prime}_{\omega}$ must then be a basis of $H^{0}(A_{\omega},L_{\omega}^{k})$ as otherwise $g_{\cal{B}^{\prime}_{\omega},k}(x_{1},\ldots,x_{c(k)})$ equals $\infty$ . But by Corollary 4.11, each $x_{i}$ retracts to the identity of $\mathbb{R}^{k}/\Lambda$ and hence lies in $V$ . By our choice of $m$ , this contradicts (27). ∎

We will apply Theorem 5.2 in the following setting: let $A$ have level $3$ structure and be defined over a discretely valued field $K$ with valuation ring $R$ , and assume that $A$ is semistable over $K$ . Let $G/R$ be the connected part of the Néron model of $A$ . Then $G$ is a semiabelian scheme over $R$ and by uniqueness of the semiabelian model [21, I.2.7], $G$ corresponds to the semiabelian scheme induced by the $R$ -point on $\overline{\cal{A}}_{g,3}$ that lifts the $K$ -point on $\cal{A}_{g,3}$ corresponding to $A$ . Hence Theorem 5.2 applies to points $x_{1},\ldots,x_{c(k)}\in A(K)$ that lift to $R$ -points of $G(R)$ .

## 6. Uniform Bounds for Semistable Principally Polarized Abelian Varieties

We now prove uniform bounds on the number of rational torsion points for ppavs of dimension $g$ for principally polarized abelian varieties $A/K$ with semistable reduction and having at least one place of bad reduction. We will actually prove a more general statement under the assumption that

$$ |S_{0}|\geq\frac{h_{\omega}(A)}{M_{0}}, $$

where $S_{0}$ is the set of places of bad reduction for $A$ and $h_{\omega}(A)$ is the Faltings height of $A$ . Then our uniform bounds will depend on $\dim A$ and $M_{0}$ . Recall from Section 2.2 that there is an ample line bundle $\omega$ on the minimal compactification $\cal{A}_{g,3}^{*}$ so that $h_{\omega}(A)$ is exactly the height of $A$ as a $K$ -point on $\cal{A}_{g,3}^{*}$ with respect to $\omega$ .

Using an analogue of analogue of Szpiro’s inequality by Deligne [32, Lemma 3.2], we can show that $M_{0}$ depends only on $g$ and $g(B)$ for $A/K$ semistable, which proves uniformity for semistable abelian varieties.

Our strategy follows that of Hindry–Silverman [61] which proves both uniform boundedness and Lang’s conjecture for elliptic curves over functions fields of characteristic $0$ . The first step is to reduce to the case where our small points $x_{i}$ reduce to the identity component of the Néron model for a uniform positive proportion of places of bad reduction. We then apply Theorems 3.1 and 5.2 to obtain a contradiction.

Given (28), we first show we can find a positive proportion of places of $S_{0}$ , depending on $M_{0}$ , such that the number of connected components for the Néron model $\cal{N}$ for these places can be uniformly bounded. To do so, we will reduce to the case of Jacobians. We first give a bound for the case of Jacobians. We note that an alternative argument is possible by using [59, Lemma 6.6] instead.

#### Proposition 6.1.

Let $C/K$ be a semistable curve of genus $g\geq 2$ and let $v\in M_{K}$ be a place such that the minimal regular model $\cal{C}/O_{K,v}$ has $N$ nodes. If $\cal{N}/O_{K,v}$ denotes the Néron model of $\operatorname{Jac}(C)$ over $K_{v}$ , then the number of connected components of its special fiber is bounded in terms of $N$ .

#### Proof.

We apply [79, Theorem 1.3]. As $C/K$ is semistable, the special fiber $\cal{C}_{s}^{\prime}$ of $\cal{C}^{\prime}$ is reduced and so we satisfy the hypothesis required. As we have $N$ nodes, it follows that the number of irreducible components of $\cal{C}^{\prime}_{s}$ is at most $N$ . We may associate to our minimal regular model a type $(n,M,R,P)$ where $n\leq N$ is the number of irreducible components, $M$ is the $n\times n$ intersection matrix $((C_{i}\cdot C_{j}))$ where the $C_{i},C_{j}$ run over the irreducible components of $\cal{C}^{\prime}_{s}$ , $R=(1,1,\ldots,1)$ as $\cal{C}^{\prime}_{s}$ is reduced, and $P=(g(C_{1}),\ldots,g(C_{n}))$ . As $\cal{C}^{\prime}$ is the minimal regular model, the numerical type must be a minimal numerical type. [108, Tag 0C9W] tells us that for a minimal type, $|(C_{i}\cdot C_{j})|$ is bounded in terms of $g$ and [108, Tag 0C9V] tells us that $g(C_{i})$ are all bounded above by $g$ . Hence there are only finitely many such minimal numerical types if $N$ is fixed. Then [79, Theorem 1.3] tells us that we can read off the number of components from a given numerical type, and so we have a uniform bound as desired. ∎

#### Proposition 6.2.

We can cover $\mathcal{A}_{g,3}$ with finitely many connected, locally closed subvarieties $Z_{1},\ldots,Z_{n}$ such that on each $Z_{i}$ there exist:

- • a smooth proper curve $C_{i}/Z_{i}$ of genus $g_{i}$ ;

- • an abelian scheme $\mathcal{B}_{i}/Z_{i}$ ;

- • a finite flat subgroup scheme $G_{i}\subseteq\mathrm{Pic}^{0}_{C_{i}/Z_{i}}$ ;

for which the quotient morphism

$$ \phi_{i}:\ \mathrm{Pic}^{0}_{C_{i}/Z_{i}}\ \twoheadrightarrow\ \mathrm{Pic}^{0}_{C_{i}/Z_{i}}/G_{i}\ \cong\ A_{Z_{i}}\times\mathcal{B}_{i} $$

is an isogeny of abelian schemes over $Z_{i}$ , where $A_{Z_{i}}$ denotes the universal abelian scheme on $\mathcal{A}_{g,3}$ restricted to $Z_{i}$ . On each $Z_{i}$ the genus is constant and satisfies

$$ g_{i}=\dim\!\big(\mathrm{Pic}^{0}_{C_{i}/Z_{i}}\big)=g+\dim(\mathcal{B}_{i})\geq g. $$

#### Proof.

Let $\mathcal{A}\to Z$ be an abelian scheme over an irreducible quasi-projective variety $Z/\mathbb{C}$ , and write $A_{K}$ for its generic fiber over $K=K(Z)$ . By Poincaré reducibility there exists a smooth proper curve $C_{K}/K$ and an abelian variety $B_{K}/K$ together with an isogeny

$$ \phi_{K}:\ \mathrm{Pic}^{0}_{C_{K}/K}\longrightarrow A_{K}\times B_{K}, $$

whose kernel $G_{K}\subseteq\mathrm{Pic}^{0}_{C_{K}/K}$ is finite. Choose a finitely generated $\mathbb{C}$ -subalgebra $R\subseteq K$ over which $C_{K}$ and $G_{K}$ descend, giving a smooth proper curve $C_{R}\to\operatorname{Spec}\,R$ and a finite subgroup scheme $G_{R}\subseteq\mathrm{Pic}^{0}_{C_{R}/R}$ .

After shrinking to a dense open $U_{0}\subseteq Z$ admitting a morphism $U_{0}\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ , we obtain a smooth proper curve $C_{U_{0}}\to U_{0}$ and a finite subgroup scheme $G_{U_{0}}\subseteq\mathrm{Pic}^{0}_{C_{U_{0}}/U_{0}}$ . Shrinking further if necessary, $G_{U_{0}}$ becomes finite flat; write $U\subseteq U_{0}$ for the resulting open and $G_{U}$ for the finite flat subgroup scheme in $\mathrm{Pic}^{0}_{C_{U}/U}$ . The quotient

$$ Q:=\mathrm{Pic}^{0}_{C_{U}/U}/G_{U} $$

exists as an abelian scheme over $U$ , and the quotient map

$$ \phi_{U}:\ \mathrm{Pic}^{0}_{C_{U}/U}\twoheadrightarrow Q $$

is a homomorphism of abelian schemes over $U$ (the structural maps to $U$ commute). By construction the generic fiber $Q_{K}$ is isomorphic to $A_{K}\times B_{K}$ . Since the functor of homomorphisms between abelian schemes is represented by an étale scheme over the base, this generic isomorphism extends, after possibly shrinking $U$ once more, to an isomorphism of abelian schemes

$$ Q\ \cong\ \mathcal{A}_{U}\times\mathcal{B}_{U}, $$

where $\mathcal{A}_{U}$ is $\mathcal{A}$ restricted to $U$ and $\mathcal{B}_{U}/U$ is an abelian scheme extending $B_{K}$ . Thus

$$ \phi_{U}:\ \mathrm{Pic}^{0}_{C_{U}/U}\longrightarrow\mathcal{A}_{U}\times\mathcal{B}_{U} $$

is an isogeny of abelian schemes over $U$ . Replacing $U$ by a connected component if necessary, the relative dimension is constant, and we have

$$ g_{U}:=\dim\!\big(\mathrm{Pic}^{0}_{C_{U}/U}\big)=\dim(\mathcal{A}_{U})+\dim(\mathcal{B}_{U})=g+\dim(\mathcal{B}_{U}), $$

so the fibers of $C_{U}/U$ have constant genus $g_{U}\geq g$ on this connected $U$ .

Applying the foregoing construction to $Z=\mathcal{A}_{g,3}$ with $\mathcal{A}$ the universal abelian scheme, we obtain a nonempty open subset $U\subseteq\mathcal{A}_{g,3}$ and, after replacing $U$ by its finitely many connected components, connected locally closed subsets $Z_{1},\dots$ on each of which we have a smooth proper curve $C_{i}/Z_{i}$ , an abelian scheme $\mathcal{B}_{i}/Z_{i}$ , and an isogeny

$$ \phi_{i}:\mathrm{Pic}^{0}_{C_{i}/Z_{i}}\longrightarrow A_{Z_{i}}\times\mathcal{B}_{i}\quad\text{over }Z_{i}. $$

On the closed complement $\mathcal{A}_{g,3}\setminus\bigcup Z_{i}$ , repeat the same construction on each irreducible component and then pass to connected components of the resulting opens. By Noetherian induction (each step removes a nonempty open from a closed subset and yields only finitely many connected components), this recursive procedure terminates after finitely many steps, giving a finite cover

$$ \mathcal{A}_{g,3}=\bigcup_{i}Z_{i} $$

by connected locally closed subvarieties possessing such data.∎

We now obtain the following proposition.

#### Proposition 6.3.

Let $A$ be a principally polarized abelian variety over a function field $K$ with $K=\mathbb{C}(B)$ and with semistable reduction. Let $M_{0}>0$ be a constant and let $S_{0}$ be the places of bad reduction for $A$ . Assume that

$$ |S_{0}|\geq\frac{h_{\omega}(A)}{M_{0}}. $$

Then there exist constants $M,k>0$ depending only on $g:=\dim A$ and $M_{0}$ , such that there is a subset $S\subseteq M_{K}$ satisfying

- (i) $A$ has bad reduction for each $v\in S$ ;

- (ii) $|S|\geq\frac{1}{M}h_{\omega}(A)$ ;

- (iii) For any $x\in A(K)$ , the point $[k]x$ lies in the identity component of the Néron model of the special fiber at each $v\in S$ .

#### Proof.

On each quasi-projective variety $Z_{i}$ from Proposition 6.2, the abelian scheme $\operatorname{Pic}^{0}_{C_{i}/Z_{i}}$ induces a map $f_{i}:Z_{i}\xhookrightarrow{}\cal{M}_{g_{i}}$ . Under this morphism $f_{i}$ , by Proposition 2.9, we have a constant $c_{i}$ such that $h_{\lambda}(f(x))\leq c_{i}h_{\omega}(x)$ for all $x\in Z_{i}(K)$ where $K$ is a global function field over $\mathbb{C}$ . Here $\lambda$ is the Hodge $\mathbb{Q}$ -line bundle on the coarse moduli space $\overline{M}_{g}$ (see Section 2.3).

Now let $A/K$ be our principally polarized abelian variety. By assumption, we have $|S_{0}|\geq\frac{1}{M^{\prime}}h_{\omega}(A)$ where $T$ is the set of bad places for $A/K$ . Let $K^{\prime}$ be a finite extension so that $A$ has level $3$ structure with $[K^{\prime}:K]$ uniformly bounded in terms of $g$ . Using $K^{\prime}$ as our reference field for global heights, we have $|S_{0}|\geq\frac{1}{M^{\prime}[K^{\prime}:K]}h_{\omega}(A)$ . Then the $K^{\prime}$ -point representing $A$ on $\cal{A}_{g,3}(K^{\prime})$ must factor through one of the $Z_{i}$ ’s of Proposition 6.2 and hence via pullback along this point we obtain a smooth proper curve $C/K^{\prime}$ such that there is an isogeny $\pi:\operatorname{Jac}(C)\to A\times A^{\prime}$ , where $A^{\prime}$ is some abelian variety and $h_{\lambda}(C)\leq ch_{\omega}(A)$ , with $\deg(\pi)$ and $c$ uniformly bounded by Proposition 2.9 since $\omega$ is an ample height. Furthermore, $g(C)$ is bounded above only in terms of $g$ .

Since $h_{\lambda}(C)\leq ch_{\omega}(A)$ , by increasing $M^{\prime}$ we also obtain

$$ |S_{0}|\geq\frac{1}{M^{\prime}[K^{\prime}:K]}h_{\lambda}(C) $$

since our constants are allowed to depend on $g$ . We replace $K^{\prime}$ with a larger extension so that $C/K^{\prime}$ has semistable reduction. We still have at least $\frac{1}{M^{\prime}[K^{\prime}:K]}h_{\lambda}(C)$ places of bad reduction for $A/K^{\prime}$ where again $[K^{\prime}:K]$ is bounded purely in terms of $g$ .

Let $S_{0}^{\prime}$ be the places of bad reduction of $A/K^{\prime}$ , so that $|S_{0}^{\prime}|\geq|T|$ . Since $h_{\lambda}(C)\geq\frac{N}{12}$ by (12), where $N$ is the total number of nodes of the minimal regular model of $C$ over $B^{\prime}$ for $B^{\prime}$ the curve corresponding to $K^{\prime}$ , it follows from (29) for at least half of these places, the number of nodes is at most $24M^{\prime}[K^{\prime}:K]$ which depends only on $g$ and $M^{\prime}$ . Let $S^{\prime}$ be these subset of $S_{0}^{\prime}$ . As $g(C)$ may be bounded above in terms of $g$ , it follows from Proposition 6.1 that for any $v\in S^{\prime}$ , the number of connected components of the special fiber of the Néron model of $\operatorname{Jac}(C)$ is at most $E$ , for some constant $E$ depending only on $g$ and $g(B)$ .

Let $x\in A(K)$ . Then since $\deg(\pi)$ is bounded solely in terms of $g$ , there exists a finite extension $L/K^{\prime}$ with $[L:K^{\prime}]$ bounded depending only on $g$ such that there is a preimage $y\in\operatorname{Jac}(C)(L)$ mapping to $x$ under $\pi_{1}$ , the projection to the first factor. Fix $w\in M_{L}$ lying over $v\in S^{\prime}$ , and set $J:=\operatorname{Jac}(C)$ and $g^{\prime}:=\dim J$ . Write

$$ \Phi_{J/K^{\prime},v}:=\text{component group of the N\'{e}ron model of }J\text{ at }v, $$

$$ \Phi_{J/L,w}:=\text{component group of the Néron model of }J\text{ at }w. $$

By [57, Thm. 5.7] one has

$$ \#\Phi_{J/L,w}\leq[L:K^{\prime}]^{g^{\prime}}\cdot\#\Phi_{J/K^{\prime},v}. $$

Using $[L:K^{\prime}]\leq n_{i}$ and the uniform bound $\#\Phi_{J/K^{\prime},v}\leq E$ for $v\in S^{\prime}$ from above, we obtain

$$ \#\Phi_{J/L,w}\leq n_{i}^{g^{\prime}}E $$

and hence

$$ \exp(\Phi_{J/L,w})\leq n_{i}^{g^{\prime}}E. $$

Let $k:=n_{i}^{g^{\prime}}E$ . Then $\exp(\Phi_{J/L,w})\mid k!$ , so for the lift $y\in J(L)$ with $\pi_{1}(y)=x$ we have $[k!]y$ reducing to the identity component of the Néron model of $J$ . at $w$ . Hence $[k!]x=\pi_{1}([k!]y)$ must lie in the identity component of $A$ over $w$ . We have thus proven our theorem by letting $S$ be the set of places of $K$ that lie below those of $S^{\prime}$ . Then

$$ |S|\geq\frac{|S^{\prime}|}{[K^{\prime}:K]}\geq\frac{|S_{0}|}{2[K^{\prime}:K]}\geq\frac{1}{2[K^{\prime}:K]^{2}M^{\prime}}h_{\omega}(A) $$

and hence we may take $M=2[K^{\prime}:K]^{2}M^{\prime}$ . ∎

Next, we cover $\cal{A}_{g,3}$ with affine opens $\{U_{i}\}$ such that on each $U_{i}$ , we have an embedding $\cal{A}_{U_{i}}\xhookrightarrow{}\mathbb{P}^{N_{i}}_{U_{i}}$ along with an extension of the endomorphism $[m_{i}]$ for some natural number $m_{i}$ .

#### Proposition 6.4.

We may cover $\cal{A}_{g,3}$ with finitely many affine opens $U_{1},\ldots,U_{m}$ such that for each $i$ , there exists an embedding $\cal{A}_{U_{i}}\xrightarrow{}\mathbb{P}^{N_{i}}_{U_{i}}$ and a natural number $m_{i}\geq 2$ such that $[m_{i}]$ extends to a morphism $f_{i}:\mathbb{P}_{U_{i}}^{N_{i}}\to\mathbb{P}_{U_{i}}^{N_{i}}$ of degree $m_{i}^{2}$ , where $\cal{A}_{U_{i}}$ is the universal abelian scheme over $U_{i}$ and $\mathbb{P}^{N_{i}}_{U_{i}}$ is projective space over $U_{i}$ .

To prove Proposition 6.4, we prove the following proposition first.

#### Proposition 6.5.

Let $S$ be a noetherian affine scheme and $\mathcal{A}/S$ an abelian scheme of relative dimension $g$ with a symmetric, rigidified, very ample line bundle $\mathcal{L}$ inducing an embedding $\mathcal{A}\hookrightarrow\mathbb{P}^{N}_{S}$ . Fix $s\in S$ and assume that

$$ \mathcal{A}_{s}\cap\{x_{0}=\cdots=x_{g}=0\}=\emptyset. $$

Suppose moreover that $\mathcal{A}$ is cut out in $\mathbb{P}^{N}_{S}$ by homogeneous polynomials of degree at most $n^{2}$ . Then there exists a Zariski neighborhood $U\subseteq S$ of $s$ such that the multiplication-by- $n$ morphism $[n]:\mathcal{A}_{U}\to\mathcal{A}_{U}$ extends to an endomorphism of $\mathbb{P}^{N}_{U}$ of degree $n^{2}$ .

#### Proof.

Let $s_{0},\dots,s_{N}$ be the sections of $\mathcal{L}$ defining the embedding $\iota:\mathcal{A}\hookrightarrow\mathbb{P}^{N}_{S}$ . Let $n\geq 1$ . Because $\mathcal{L}$ is symmetric, the theorem of the cube gives an isomorphism

$$ [n]^{*}\mathcal{L}\cong\mathcal{L}^{\otimes n^{2}}\otimes(e^{*}\mathcal{L})^{\otimes\binom{n}{2}}, $$

where $e:S\to\mathcal{A}$ is the identity section. As $\mathcal{L}$ is rigidified, $e^{*}\mathcal{L}\cong\mathcal{O}_{S}$ , so we obtain a canonical isomorphism $[n]^{*}\mathcal{L}\cong\mathcal{L}^{\otimes n^{2}}$ . In particular, for each $j$ the pullback $[n]^{*}s_{j}$ is a section of $\mathcal{L}^{\otimes n^{2}}$ . Since $H^{0}(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{L}^{\otimes n^{2}})$ is generated by degree- $n^{2}$ monomials in the $s_{i}$ , we may choose a homogeneous polynomial $f_{j}(s_{0},\dots,s_{N})$ of degree $n^{2}$ representing $[n]^{*}s_{j}$ . These $f_{j}$ are unique only modulo the homogeneous ideal of $\mathcal{A}$ .

The tuple $(f_{0},\dots,f_{N})$ defines a rational map $F:\mathbb{P}^{N}_{S}\dashrightarrow\mathbb{P}^{N}_{S}$ , and by construction $F$ restricts to multiplication by $n$ on $\mathcal{A}$ . Indeed, for $T$ an $S$ -scheme and $a\in\mathcal{A}(T)$ , the image of $a$ under the embedding $\iota:\mathcal{A}\hookrightarrow\mathbb{P}^{N}_{S}$ is

$$ \iota(a)=[s_{0}(a):\cdots:s_{N}(a)]\in\mathbb{P}^{N}(T). $$

Write $[n]:\mathcal{A}\to\mathcal{A}$ for the multiplication-by- $n$ morphism. Then

$$ \iota([n](a))=[s_{0}([n](a)):\cdots:s_{N}([n](a))]. $$

By definition of pullback of sections,

$$ s_{j}([n](a))=([n]^{*}s_{j})(a)=f_{j}(s_{0}(a),\dots,s_{N}(a)). $$

Thus

$$ \iota([n](a))=(f_{0}(s_{0}(a),\dots,s_{N}(a)),\dots,f_{N}(s_{0}(a),\dots,s_{N}(a))), $$

as claimed.

To extend $F$ to a morphism on some neighborhood $U\subseteq S$ of $s$ , we must arrange that the $f_{j}$ have no common zeroes on $\mathbb{P}^{N}_{U}$ . The hypothesis

$$ \mathcal{A}_{s}\cap\{x_{0}=\cdots=x_{g}=0\}=\emptyset $$

says that $s_{0},\dots,s_{g}$ have no common zero on $\mathcal{A}_{s}$ . Passing to the embedding associated to $\mathcal{L}^{\otimes n^{2}}$ if necessary, the pullback sections $[n]^{*}s_{0},\dots,[n]^{*}s_{N}$ provide the projective coordinates in this embedding. Each $[n]^{*}s_{j}$ can be represented by a homogeneous polynomial $f_{j}(s_{0},\dots,s_{N})$ of degree $n^{2}$ , unique only modulo the homogeneous ideal of $\mathcal{A}$ . By choosing these representatives $f_{0},\dots,f_{g}$ suitably, we may ensure that their common zero locus in $\mathbb{P}^{N}_{s}$ , where $\mathbb{P}^{N}_{s}$ is the fiber above $s$ , has codimension $g+1$ . This furnishes the base case of the induction.

We now follow Fakhruddin’s argument in [38, Proposition 2.1]. Suppose inductively that for some $i\geq 0$ the common vanishing locus

$$ Y_{s}=\{f_{0}=\cdots=f_{g+i}=0\}\subseteq\mathbb{P}^{N}_{s} $$

has codimension $g+i+1$ . To define $f_{g+i+1}$ , choose a homogeneous polynomial $h_{1}$ of degree $n^{2}$ restricting to $[n]^{*}s_{g+i+1}$ on $\mathcal{A}$ , and choose another homogeneous polynomial $h_{2}$ of degree $n^{2}$ vanishing on $\mathcal{A}$ but not identically on any irreducible component of $Y_{s}$ (this is possible since $Y_{s}\cap\mathcal{A}_{s}=\varnothing$ ). For general $b$ , the linear combination $f_{g+i+1}=h_{1}+b\,h_{2}$ still restricts to $[n]^{*}s_{g+i+1}$ on $\mathcal{A}$ and avoids vanishing identically on any component of $Y_{s}$ , so the new common vanishing locus

$$ \{f_{0}=\cdots=f_{g+i+1}=0\} $$

has codimension $g+i+2$ .

Iterating, we obtain $f_{0},\dots,f_{N}$ whose common zero locus in $\mathbb{P}^{N}_{s}$ is empty. Equivalently, the resultant $\operatorname{Res}(f_{0},\dots,f_{N})$ is nonzero in the residue field of $s$ , hence invertible on some Zariski open neighborhood $U$ of $s$ . Over $U$ , the polynomials $f_{0},\dots,f_{N}$ therefore define a genuine morphism

$$ F:\mathbb{P}^{N}_{U}\to\mathbb{P}^{N}_{U} $$

of degree $n^{2}$ whose restriction to $\mathcal{A}_{U}$ coincides with $[n]$ .∎

#### Proof of Proposition 6.4.

For each $x$ , let $U_{x}$ be an affine open containing $x$ . If $\cal{L}$ is the universal line bundle on $\cal{A}_{g,3}$ , then as $\cal{L}^{3}$ is very ample we can embed $\cal{A}_{U_{x}}\xhookrightarrow{}\mathbb{P}^{N}_{U_{x}}$ as a closed subscheme. By Bertini we can arrange the embedding so that $\cal{A}_{x}\cap\{x_{0}=\cdots=x_{g}=0\}$ is empty. By noetherianess, there is some $n_{x}>0$ for which it is cut out by homogeneous polynomials of degree at most $n_{x}^{2}$ . Proposition 6.5 implies that after shrinking $U_{x}$ , the morphism $[n_{x}]$ extends to $\mathbb{P}^{N}_{U_{x}}$ and furthermore after picking some homogeneous lift $F$ of the morphism $f$ , we may assume that $F$ has an invertible coefficient too. We can then multiply $F$ by the inverse of this coefficient and assume that it is $1$ . Now by compactness of $\mathcal{A}_{g,3}$ , we can find finitely many such affine opens as desired.∎

Given $g\geq 1$ , we fix once and for all a finite cover $\{U_{i}\}$ by open affines $U_{i}$ of $\mathcal{A}_{g,3}$ as in Proposition 6.4, as well as the associated integers $m_{i},N_{i}$ that arise as the extensions of $[m_{i}]$ to $\mathbb{P}_{U_{i}}^{N_{i}}$ . We thus consider all dependencies on these $U_{i},m_{i},N_{i}$ to constitute a dependence only on $g$ . Observe that on each $U_{i}$ we obtain a morphism $\varphi_{i}:U_{i}\to\operatorname{Rat}^{N_{i}}_{m_{i}^{2}}$ extending $[m_{i}]$ , and as both $U_{i}$ and $\operatorname{Rat}^{N_{i}}_{m_{i}^{2}}$ are affine, it follows from Proposition 2.9 that there exists a $c_{i}>0$ such that

$$ c_{i}h_{\partial U_{i}}(A)\geq h(\varphi_{i}(A)) $$

where $h$ is the Weil height on $\operatorname{Rat}^{N_{i}}_{m_{i}^{2}}$ . Indeed, as $U_{i}$ is affine, we may choose a compactification $\overline{U}_{i}$ such that $\partial U_{i}=\overline{U}_{i}\setminus U_{i}$ is ample. To do so, we embed $U_{i}$ into $\mathbb{A}^{k}$ for some $k>0$ and then choose its closure $\overline{U}_{i}\subseteq\mathbb{P}^{k}$ as the compactification. Since $\mathbb{P}^{k}\setminus\mathbb{A}^{k}$ is an ample divisor on $\mathbb{P}^{k}$ , so is its restriction $\overline{U}_{i}\setminus U_{i}$ to $\overline{U}_{i}$ .

On the other hand, we may choose compactifications $U_{i}^{*}$ in $\cal{A}_{g,3}^{*}=\overline{X}$ . By Proposition 2.7, there is some $\eta\geq 1$ such that

$$ \eta^{-1}\lambda_{\overline{U}_{i}\setminus U_{i}}\leq\lambda_{U_{i}^{*}\setminus U_{i}}\leq\eta\lambda_{\overline{U}_{i}\setminus U_{i}}. $$

We may therefore without loss set $\partial U_{i}$ to be $U_{i}^{*}\setminus U_{i}$ and assume that (30) holds for $h_{\partial U_{i}}$ .

Since $\{U_{i}\}$ is a finite cover of $X=\cal{A}_{g,3}$ , for any compactification $\overline{X}$ of $X$ we have

$$ \partial U_{1}\cap\partial U_{2}\cap\cdots\cap\partial U_{m}=\partial X $$

and thus by (6),

$$ \min\{\lambda_{\partial U_{1}},\ldots,\lambda_{\partial U_{m}}\}=\lambda_{\partial X}. $$

Hence for any $K$ -point $A$ of $X$ where $K$ is a complete algebraically closed field with $\mathbb{C}$ a trivially valued subfield, there exists some $i$ such that

$$ \lambda_{\partial U_{i}}(A)\leq\lambda_{\partial X}(A). $$

We are now ready to prove the following theorem.

#### Theorem 6.6.

Let $K=\mathbb{C}(B)$ be the function field of a smooth projective curve $B$ over $\mathbb{C}$ , and let $A/K$ be a principally polarized abelian variety with semistable reduction. Assume there exists a constant $M_{0}>0$ such that

$$ |S_{0}|\geq\frac{h_{\omega}(A)}{M_{0}} $$

where $S_{0}$ is the set of places of bad reduction for $A$ . Then there are positive constants $n=n(\mathrm{dim}(A),M_{0})$ and $\varepsilon=\varepsilon(\dim A,M_{0})$ such that if $h_{\omega}(A)>0$ , then

$$ \{x\in A(K)\mid\widehat{h}_{A}(x)\leq\varepsilon h_{\operatorname{Fal}}(A)\} $$

is contained in $\operatorname{div}(s)$ for some nonzero $s\in H^{0}(A,L^{n})$ , where $L$ is the symmetric ample line bundle inducing the principal polarization on $A$ and $\widehat{h}_{A}$ denotes the Néron–Tate height with respect to $L$ .

#### Proof.

We may pass to an extension $K^{\prime}/K$ with $[K^{\prime}:K]$ bounded in terms of $g$ so that $A$ attains level $3$ structure. Let $S$ be the set of places provided by Proposition 6.3 and let $S^{\prime}$ be the set of places in $K^{\prime}$ that is over $S$ . Then for all $v\in S$ , $A$ has bad reduction at $v$ , and we have $M,k>0$ , depending only on $M_{0}$ and $\dim A$ , such that

$$ |S|\geq\frac{1}{M}h_{\omega}(A) $$

and $[k]x$ reduces to the identity component of the Néron model over $v$ for all $x\in A(K)$ .

We now consider all global heights with respect to $K^{\prime}$ , so that $h_{\omega}(A)$ is scaled by a factor of $[K^{\prime}:K]$ . Then we have the inequality

$$ |S^{\prime}|\geq\frac{1}{M[K^{\prime}:K]}h_{\omega}(A). $$

For each $v\in K^{\prime}$ , let $x_{v}$ be the induced point on $\cal{A}_{g,3}(K_{v}^{\prime})$ by $A$ . For each $v\in S^{\prime}$ , we see from (31) that there exists $i_{v}$ such that $x_{v}\in U_{i_{v}}$ and

$$ \lambda_{\partial U_{i_{v}}}(x_{v})\leq c\lambda_{\partial X}(x_{v}). $$

Since there are $m$ such opens, there exists a subset $\Sigma\subseteq S^{\prime}$ consisting of at least $\frac{|S^{\prime}|}{m}$ places such that they share the same such $i=i_{v}$ , say $i=1$ .

Note that the $K^{\prime}$ -point of $\mathcal{A}_{g,3}$ given by $A$ lies in $U_{1}$ . By Proposition 6.4, we have an embedding $\cal{A}_{U_{1}}\xhookrightarrow{}\mathbb{P}_{U_{1}}^{N}$ with an endomorphism $f:\mathbb{P}_{U_{1}}^{N}\to\mathbb{P}_{U_{1}}^{N}$ extending $[m_{1}]$ for some $m_{1}\geq 2$ , along with a fixed homogeneous lift $F:\mathbb{A}_{U_{1}}^{N+1}\to\mathbb{A}_{U_{1}}^{N+1}$ with one of its coefficients being $1$ . For each $n\geq 1$ , fix a good basis $\cal{B}_{n}\subseteq H^{0}(A,L^{n})$ over $K^{\prime}$ with respect to this lift $F$ . Then since one of the coefficients of $F$ is equal to $1$ , we have (19) and therefore (20). Since by (30) there exists a $c_{1}>0$ such that

$$ c_{1}h_{\partial U_{1}}(A)\geq h(f), $$

(20) gives us a constant $C>0$ (depending only on $g$ ) such that for any $T\subseteq M_{K^{\prime}}$ and any $x_{1},\ldots,x_{c(n)}\in A(K^{\prime})$ , we have

$$ \sum_{v\in T}g_{\cal{B}_{n},v}(x_{1},\ldots,x_{c(n)})\geq-\frac{C\log n}{n}h_{\partial U_{1}}(A)+\sum_{v\in T}r_{v}(F) $$

where $g_{\cal{B}_{n},v}$ is the Arakelov-Green’s function over the non-archimedean field $K_{v}$ , and $r_{v}(F)$ equals (13) with absolute value $|\cdot|_{v}$ . We will choose $T$ later. Let $h:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ be an increasing function such that for all $n\in\mathbb{N}$ , $h(n)=c(k)$ for some $k$ ; we fix the properties of $h$ later. Then by (33) along with Theorem 5.2, there exists a nonempty finite list $\{n_{1},\ldots,n_{m^{\prime}}\}$ such that any $A/K^{\prime}_{v}$ with bad reduction is $n_{i}$ -good for some $1\leq i\leq m^{\prime}$ . If we write $h(n)=c(k_{n})$ and choose our function $h$ so that

$$ \sum_{i=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{k_{i}^{1/2}}<1, $$

then in particular

$$ \sum_{i=1}^{m^{\prime}}\frac{1}{k_{n_{i}}^{1/2}}<1. $$

We now claim that there is an $1\leq i\leq m^{\prime}$ such that for at least $\frac{1}{k_{n_{i}}^{1/2}}|\Sigma|$ places $v\in\Sigma$ , the abelian variety $A/K_{v}^{\prime}$ is $n_{i}$ -good. Otherwise, for each $1\leq i\leq m^{\prime}$ , there are at most $\frac{|\Sigma|}{k_{n_{i}}^{1/2}}$ places of $\Sigma$ such that $A$ is $n_{i}$ -good. Since for every $v\in\Sigma$ , we have that $A/K^{\prime}$ is $n_{i}$ good for some $1\leq i\leq m^{\prime}$ , it follows that

$$ \sum_{i=1}^{m^{\prime}}\frac{|\Sigma|}{k_{n_{i}}^{1/2}}\geq|\Sigma|, $$

and hence

$$ \sum_{i=1}^{m^{\prime}}\frac{1}{k_{n_{i}}^{1/2}}\geq 1, $$

which contradicts (35). Thus there is an $1\leq i\leq m^{\prime}$ such that for at least $\frac{1}{k_{n_{i}}^{1/2}}|\Sigma|$ places $v\in\Sigma$ , the abelian variety $A/K_{v}^{\prime}$ is $n_{i}$ -good. We assume without loss that $i=1$ , so that at least $\frac{|\Sigma|}{k_{n_{1}}^{1/2}}$ of the places of $\Sigma$ are $n_{1}$ -good. Let $\Sigma^{\prime}$ be this subset of places, which by assumption satisfies

$$ |\Sigma^{\prime}|\geq\frac{1}{k_{n_{1}}^{1/2}}|\Sigma|. $$

Now assume we are given $x_{1},\ldots,x_{c(k_{n_{1}})}\in A(K^{\prime})$ that all reduce to the identity component of the Néron model for all $v\in\Sigma^{\prime}$ . As $A/K_{v}$ is $n_{1}$ -good, we obtain

$$ g_{\cal{B}_{k_{n_{1}}},v}(x_{1},\ldots,x_{c(k_{n_{1}})})\geq\frac{1}{n_{1}}\lambda_{\partial U_{1}}(A_{v})+r_{v}(F)\geq\frac{1}{n_{1}}+r(F_{v}) $$

since $\lambda_{\partial U_{1}}(A_{v})\geq\lambda_{\partial\cal{A}_{g,3}}\geq 1$ . Here, the second equality follows from the fact that $\lambda_{\partial\cal{A}_{g,3}}(A_{v})>0$ due to having bad reduction and that $\lambda_{\partial\cal{A}_{g,3}}:\cal{A}_{g,3}(K^{\prime}_{v})\to\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ is valued in non-negative integers as we take $K^{\prime}$ to be our base field. Recalling that $\sum_{v\in M_{K^{\prime}}}r_{v}(F)=0$ , we now sum over all places in $M_{K^{\prime}}$ using (34) and (37). Letting $T=M_{K^{\prime}}\setminus\Sigma^{\prime}$ in (34), we obtain

$$ \sum_{v\in M_{K^{\prime}}}g_{\cal{B}_{k_{n_{1}}},v}(x_{1},\ldots,x_{c(k_{n_{1}})})\geq\frac{1}{n_{1}}|\Sigma^{\prime}|-\frac{C\log k_{n_{1}}}{k_{n_{1}}}h_{\partial U_{1}}(A). $$

By (32) and the fact that $\omega$ is ample on the minimal compactification $\mathcal{A}_{g,3}^{*}$ combined with Proposition 2.8, we have

$$ |\Sigma|\geq\frac{1}{mM[K^{\prime}:K]}h_{\omega}(A)\geq\frac{1}{M^{\prime}}h_{\partial U_{1}}(A) $$

for some constant $M^{\prime}$ depending only on $g$ and $g(B)$ . Combining (38) and (39) with (36), we get

$$ \sum_{v\in M_{K^{\prime}}}g_{\cal{B}_{k_{n_{1}}},v}(x_{1},\ldots,x_{c(k_{n_{1}})})\geq\left(\frac{1}{M^{\prime}n_{1}k_{n_{1}}^{1/2}}-\frac{C\log k_{n_{1}}}{k_{n_{1}}}\right)h_{\partial U_{1}}(A). $$

Now note that $M^{\prime}$ and $C$ depend only on $g$ and $g(B)$ . Hence there are constants $C^{\prime}$ and $\delta>0$ depending only on $g$ and $g(B)$ such that if $2C^{\prime}n_{1}^{3}\geq k_{n_{1}}\geq C^{\prime}n_{1}^{3}$ , then

$$ \sum_{v\in M_{K^{\prime}}}g_{\cal{B}_{k_{n_{1}}},v}(x_{1},\ldots,x_{c(k_{n_{1}})})\geq\delta h_{\partial U_{1}}(A). $$

We now choose $k_{i}$ for our function $h$ that satisfy

$$ 2C^{\prime}i^{3}\geq k_{i}\geq C^{\prime}i^{3} $$

for all $i\in\mathbb{N}$ , so that in particular (40) always holds. Suppose $\widehat{h}_{A}(x_{i})\leq\varepsilon h_{\operatorname{Fal}}(A)$ . Then unless $g_{\cal{B}_{k_{n_{1}}},v}(x_{1},\ldots,x_{c(k_{n_{1}})})=+\infty$ , we must have

$$ \sum_{v\in M_{K^{\prime}}}g_{\cal{B}_{k_{n_{1}}},v}(x_{1},\ldots,x_{c(k_{n_{1}})})\leq\varepsilon h_{\operatorname{Fal}}(A). $$

On the other hand, by Proposition 2.9, since $h_{\operatorname{Fal}}(A)=h_{\omega}(A)$ and $\omega$ is an ample line bundle on $\cal{A}_{g,3}^{*}$ , there is some $c^{\prime}>0$ depending only on $g$ such that $h_{\partial U_{1}}(A)\geq c^{\prime}h_{\operatorname{Fal}}(A)$ . Hence (41) yields a contradiction with (40) for all $\varepsilon\ll_{g,g(B)}1$ . Thus $g_{\cal{B}_{k_{n_{1}}},v}(x_{1},\ldots,x_{c(k_{n_{1}})})=\infty$ . This means that there must exist some nonzero $s\in H^{0}(A,L^{k_{n_{1}}})$ such that $x_{1},\dots,x_{c(k_{n_{1}})}$ all lie on $\operatorname{div}(s)$ . Therefore, for any set of $c(k_{n_{1}})$ torsion points in $A(K^{\prime})$ that reduce to the identity component for all $v\in\Sigma^{\prime}$ , there must be a nonzero section $s\in H^{0}(A,L^{k_{n_{1}}})$ such that these points all lie on $\div(s)$ .

We conclude that for any set of points $x_{1},\dots,x_{N_{0}}$ (independent of $N_{0}$ ) defined over $K^{\prime}$ of Néron–Tate height at most $\varepsilon h_{\operatorname{Fal}}(A)$ which all reduce to the identity component of the Néron model for all $v\in S^{\prime}$ , there must exist a nonzero $s\in H^{0}(A,L^{k_{n_{1}}})$ such that the $x_{i}$ all lie on $\operatorname{div}(s)$ . Indeed, otherwise the rectangular matrix formed by $\det(\eta_{j}(\tilde{x}_{i}))_{\eta_{j}\in\mathcal{B}_{k_{n_{1}}}}$ has rank $c(k_{n_{1}})$ . If $N_{0}<c(k_{n_{1}})$ then this clearly cannot happen. If $N_{0}\geq c(k_{n_{1}})$ , then it follows that we can find a $c(k_{n_{1}})\times c(k_{n_{1}})$ minor of maximal rank and thus that there does not exist any nonzero $s\in H^{0}(A,L^{k_{n_{1}}})$ such that the $x_{i}$ all lie on $\operatorname{div}(s)$ , contradicting the preceding argument.

Each place $v\in\Sigma^{\prime}$ lies above some $v\in S$ , where $S$ is as in Proposition 6.3. In particular if $x\in A(K)$ , then $[k]x$ reduces to the identity component for all $v\in S$ . Hence given any set of points $x_{1},\ldots,x_{c(N_{0})}\in A(K)$ with $\widehat{h}_{A}(x_{i})\leq\frac{\varepsilon}{k^{2}}h_{\operatorname{Fal}}(A)$ , there must be a nonzero $s\in H^{0}(A,L^{k_{n_{1}}})$ such that $[k]x_{1},\ldots,[k]x_{N_{0}}$ all lie on $\operatorname{div}(s)$ , and hence $x_{1},\ldots,x_{N_{0}}$ all lie on $[k]^{*}(\operatorname{div}(s))\in H^{0}(A,L^{k_{n_{1}}k^{2}})$ . Our theorem is thus proven by taking $n=k_{n_{1}}k^{2}$ . ∎

We now note that Theorem 6.6 is enough to imply the case of semistable abelian varieties with at least one place of bad reduction, where the constants only depend on the dimension $g$ and the genus $g(B)$ .

#### Corollary 6.7.

Let $K=\mathbb{C}(B)$ be the function field of a smooth projective curve $B$ over $\mathbb{C}$ , and let $A/K$ be a principally polarized abelian variety with semistable reduction. Then there are positive constants $n=n(\mathrm{dim}(A),g(B))$ and $\varepsilon=\varepsilon(\dim A,g(B))$ such that if $A$ has at least one place of bad reduction, then

$$ \{x\in A(K)\mid\widehat{h}_{A}(x)\leq\varepsilon h_{\operatorname{Fal}}(A)\} $$

is contained in $\operatorname{div}(s)$ for some nonzero section $s\in H^{0}(A,L^{n})$ , where $L$ is the symmetric ample line bundle inducing the principal polarization and $\widehat{h}_{A}$ denotes the Néron–Tate height with respect to $L$ .

#### Proof.

Since $A$ has at least one place of bad reduction, we have $h_{\omega}(A)>0$ . We now have to show that there is a constant $M_{0}$ , depending only on $g$ and $g(B)$ , such that

$$ |S_{0}|\geq\frac{h_{\omega}(A)}{M_{0}} $$

where $S_{0}$ is the set of places of bad reduction for $A$ . By [32, Lemma 3.2], as $A/K$ has semistable reduction, we know that

$$ h_{\omega}(A)\leq\frac{g}{2}(2g(B)-2+|S_{0}|) $$

if $2g(B)-2+|S_{0}|\geq 0$ . This gives us our desired constant $M_{0}$ if $g(B)\geq 1$ . If $g(B)=0$ , then the only case in which we are not done is if $|S_{0}|=1$ . But as $\cal{A}_{g}$ is hyperbolic, any map from $\mathbb{C}$ to it must be a constant map and so $|S_{0}|=0$ in this case and we do not have any place of bad reduction, which contradicts our hypotheses. ∎

## 7. Néron Models for Potential Good Reduction

In this section, we study the Néron model $\cal{N}$ for an abelian variety $A/K$ with potential good reduction. If $K^{\prime}/K$ is a finite extension for which $A/K^{\prime}$ has good reduction with abelian scheme $\cal{A}^{\prime}/R^{\prime}$ , then we are interested in bounding the degree of the image of the special fiber of $\cal{N}$ when mapped to $\cal{A}^{\prime}$ using the universal property of Néron models. This will essentially follow from results of Edixhoven [35] which are reinterpreted in Halle–Nicaise [58].

Let $K$ be a non-archimedean field with a discrete valuation and having residue characteristic zero. Let $A/K$ be an abelian variety with potential good reduction. This means that over some finite extension $K^{\prime}/K$ , the abelian variety $A_{K^{\prime}}/K^{\prime}$ extends to an abelian scheme $\cal{A}^{\prime}/R^{\prime}$ where $R^{\prime}$ is the valuation ring of $K^{\prime}$ . In fact we may take $K^{\prime}=K(A[3])$ .

If $R$ is the valuation ring of $R^{\prime}$ , then we still have a Néron model $\cal{N}/R$ for $A/K$ . Then the base change $\cal{N}_{R^{\prime}}$ is a smooth model for $A_{K^{\prime}}$ and hence by the universal property of Néron models, there must be a $R^{\prime}$ -morphism $f:\cal{N}_{R^{\prime}}\to\cal{A}^{\prime}$ . We now assume that the residue field of $K$ is algebraically closed, so that $K^{\prime}/K$ is totally ramified and $K^{\prime}$ and $K$ have isomorphic residue fields. In particular, passing to special fibers we obtain a morphism

$$ f_{s}:\cal{N}_{s}\to\cal{A}^{\prime}_{s}. $$

We are interested in understanding the image $f(\cal{N}_{s})$ inside $\cal{A}^{\prime}_{s}$ . To do so, we will apply [58, Lemma 3.2]. We summarize the setup below.

Since $K^{\prime}/K$ is totally ramified, if $d=[K^{\prime}:K]$ then we may identify $\operatorname{Gal}(K^{\prime}/K)$ with $\mu_{d}$ , the group of $d$ th roots of unity. By the Néron mapping property, the action of $\mu_{d}$ on $A^{\prime}/K^{\prime}$ extends to the abelian scheme $\cal{A}^{\prime}/R^{\prime}$ ; this action is equivariant with respect to $\cal{A}^{\prime}\to\operatorname{Spec}R^{\prime}$ and hence induces an action on the special fiber $\cal{A}^{\prime}_{s}$ .

#### Proposition 7.1.

The morphism $f_{s}:\cal{N}_{s}\to\cal{A}^{\prime}_{s}$ factors through the fixed part $(\cal{A}^{\prime}_{s})^{\mu_{d}}$ and is surjective onto $(\cal{A}^{\prime}_{s})^{\mu_{d}}$ .

#### Proof.

This is [58, Lemma 3.2 (2)]. ∎

Now let’s assume that $A$ has bad reduction over $K$ . This means that the special fiber $\cal{N}_{s}$ of the Néron model is not an abelian variety. The identity component $(\cal{N}_{s})^{0}$ factors as

$$ 1\to U\to(\cal{N}_{s})^{0}\to C\to 1 $$

where $U$ is a commutative unipotent group and $C$ an abelian variety of dimension $<\dim A$ . As any morphism from $U$ to $\cal{A}^{\prime}_{s}$ must be trivial, the map $f_{s}\mid_{(\cal{N}_{s})^{0}}:(\cal{N}_{s})^{0}\to\cal{A}_{s}^{\prime}$ must factor through $C$ . As the image of $C$ under the induced map to $\cal{A}_{s}^{\prime}$ must be a proper abelian subvariety of $\cal{A}_{s}^{\prime}$ , it follows that $f_{s}(\cal{N}_{s})$ is a finite union of translates of $B$ .

We seek to bound the degree of $(\cal{A}^{\prime}_{s})^{\mu_{d}}$ . Fix a line bundle as follows. Let $L$ be a line bundle for $A/K$ which is naturally a line bundle for $A_{K^{\prime}}/K^{\prime}$ . This extends to a unique line bundle $\cal{L}$ for the abelian scheme $\cal{A}^{\prime}/R^{\prime}$ as $R^{\prime}$ is a DVR and $\operatorname{Pic}(R^{\prime})=0$ [15, Theorem 8.4.3]. We thus get a line bundle $\cal{L}_{s}$ on $\cal{A}^{\prime}_{s}$ .

#### Proposition 7.2.

For $g\in\mu_{d}$ , we have an isomorphism $g^{*}\cal{L}_{s}\simeq\cal{L}_{s}$ .

#### Proof.

We have $g^{*}(\cal{L}_{s})=(g^{*}\cal{L})_{s}$ since the action on the special fiber is induced by that on $\cal{A}^{\prime}$ . The generic fiber of $g^{*}\cal{L}$ is equal to $g^{*}L$ which is isomorphic to $L$ itself since $L$ was defined over $K$ . As $g^{*}\cal{L}$ is the unique line bundle lifting $g^{*}L$ , we must have $g^{*}\cal{L}\simeq\cal{L}$ and thus

$$ g^{*}(\cal{L}_{s})=(g^{*}\cal{L})_{s}\simeq\cal{L}_{s}. $$

∎

We now bound $\deg_{\cal{L}_{s}}((\cal{A}_{s})^{\mu_{d}})$ . We will prove the following general proposition that bounds $\deg_{L}(X^{G})$ for a finite group $G$ acting on a projective variety $X$ and $L$ is an ample line bundle which is $G$ -invariant, i.e., which satisfies $g^{*}L\simeq L$ for all $g\in G$ .

#### Proposition 7.3.

Let $X$ be a projective variety of dimension $d$ over an algebraically closed field $k$ , and let $G$ be a finite group acting on $X$ by automorphisms. For a very ample line bundle $L$ on $X$ , denote by $\deg_{L}(\cdot)$ the degree with respect to $L$ , and let

$$ X^{G}:=\{x\in X:g(x)=x\text{ for all }g\in G\} $$

be the fixed-point subvariety. Assume that $g^{*}L$ and $L$ have the same numerical class for all $g\in G$ . Then

$$ \deg_{L}(X^{G})\leq|G^{\mathrm{ab}}||G|^{d}\deg_{L}(X). $$

#### Proof.

Fix once and for all an ordering $G=\{a_{1},\dots,a_{n}\}$ , and set

$$ M=\bigotimes_{i=1}^{n}a_{i}^{*}L. $$

For $g\in G$ we compute

$$ g^{*}M=g^{*}\Big(\bigotimes_{i=1}^{n}a_{i}^{*}L\Big)=\bigotimes_{i=1}^{n}g^{*}(a_{i}^{*}L)=\bigotimes_{i=1}^{n}(a_{i}\circ g)^{*}L. $$

Since $i\mapsto a_{i}\circ g$ permutes $\{a_{1},\dots,a_{n}\}$ , there is a canonical permutation isomorphism

$$ \psi_{g}:g^{*}M\longrightarrow M $$

defined by sending each factor $(a_{i}\circ g)^{*}L$ of $g^{*}M$ to the unique slot in $M=\bigotimes_{j=1}^{n}a_{j}^{*}L$ labeled by the same $a_{j}$ . In this way $\psi_{g}$ restores the fixed reference order $(a_{1},\dots,a_{n})$ in the codomain.

Fix $g,h\in G$ . We compare two maps $(hg)^{*}M\to M$ . First, we have

$$ \psi_{hg}:(hg)^{*}M=g^{*}\big(\bigotimes_{i=1}^{n}(a_{i}\circ h)^{*}L\big)=\bigotimes_{i=1}^{n}(a_{i}\circ h\circ g)^{*}L\xrightarrow[t=a_{i}\circ h\circ g]{}\bigotimes_{t\in G}t^{*}L=M, $$

where the reindexing sends each factor $(a_{i}\circ h\circ g)^{*}L$ to the unique slot of $M=\bigotimes_{j=1}^{n}a_{j}^{*}L$ labeled by $a_{j}=t=a_{i}\circ h\circ g$ , thereby restoring the fixed order.

Second, consider

$$ \psi_{g}\circ g^{*}\psi_{h}:(hg)^{*}M=g^{*}h^{*}M\xrightarrow{g^{*}\psi_{h}}g^{*}M\xrightarrow{\psi_{g}}M. $$

Here $g^{*}\psi_{h}$ is the map

$$ g^{*}h^{*}M=\bigotimes_{i=1}^{n}(a_{i}\circ h\circ g)^{*}L\longrightarrow g^{*}M=\bigotimes_{j=1}^{n}(a_{j}\circ g)^{*}L $$

obtained by reindexing via $a_{j}=a_{i}\circ h$ , i.e. sending the factor $(a_{i}\circ h\circ g)^{*}L$ to the factor $(a_{j}\circ g)^{*}L$ . Then $\psi_{g}$ reindexes $g^{*}M=\bigotimes_{j=1}^{n}(a_{j}\circ g)^{*}L$ by $t=a_{j}\circ g$ to identify it with $M=\bigotimes_{t\in G}t^{*}L$ , again by sending each factor to the unique slot labeled by the same $a_{j}$ and restoring the fixed order. Thus both constructions carry each factor $(a_{i}\circ h\circ g)^{*}L$ of $(hg)^{*}M$ to the slot of $M$ labeled by $a_{j}=a_{i}\circ h\circ g$ , and hence

$$ \psi_{hg}=\psi_{g}\circ g^{*}\psi_{h}. $$

Define $T_{g}:H^{0}(X,M)\to H^{0}(X,M)$ by $(T_{g}s)(x)=(\psi_{g})_{x}((g^{*}s)(x))$ . By (43), for $s\in H^{0}(X,M)$ ,

$$ (T_{g}T_{h}s)(x)=(\psi_{g})_{x}((g^{*}(T_{h}s))(x))=((\psi_{g}\circ g^{*}\psi_{h})_{x})(((hg)^{*}s)(x)) $$

$$ =(\psi_{hg})_{x}(((hg)^{*}s)(x))=(T_{hg}s)(x). $$

Thus $g\mapsto T_{g}$ is a right action: $T_{g}T_{h}=T_{hg}$ . If a left representation is desired, set $S_{g}:=T_{g^{-1}}$ , then $S_{g}S_{h}=S_{gh}$ . Either way, $H^{0}(X,M)$ carries a representation of $G$ .

As $L$ is very ample, it follows that $a_{i}^{*}L$ is also very ample and hence $M$ is very ample. The complete linear system of $M$ defines a closed embedding

$$ \iota:X\longrightarrow\mathbb{P}(H^{0}(X,M)^{\vee})=:\mathbb{P}^{N}, $$

where $\iota(x)$ is the point of $\mathbb{P}(H^{0}(X,M)^{\vee})$ corresponding to the line of functionals $\{\ell\mapsto\ell(s(x)):s\in H^{0}(X,M)\}$ . Write $V:=H^{0}(X,M)$ and $W:=V^{\vee}$ . Both are finite-dimensional vector spaces over $k$ . The action of $G$ on $V$ induces the dual action on $W$ , hence a projective action on $\mathbb{P}(W)$ defined as follows: if $0\neq w\in W$ , then the corresponding point of $\mathbb{P}(W)$ is the line $\{\ell w:\ell\in k\}\subseteq W$ , and we set

$$ g\cdot\{\ell w:\ell\in k\}:=\{\ell(g\cdot w):\ell\in k\}. $$

With this action the embedding $\iota$ is readily checked to be $G$ -equivariant.

A point $\{\ell w:\ell\in k\}\in\mathbb{P}(W)$ is fixed by $G$ exactly when for each $g\in G$ the vectors $w$ and $g\cdot w$ lie in the same one-dimensional subspace of $W$ . Equivalently, for each $g\in G$ there exists a scalar $\chi(g)\in k^{\times}$ such that $g\cdot w=\chi(g)w$ , where the left-hand side uses the dual action of $G$ on $W$ defined above. This condition precisely says that the line $\{\ell w:\ell\in k\}$ is a one-dimensional $G$ -subrepresentation of $W$ . The assignment $\chi:G\to k^{\times}$ , $g\mapsto\chi(g)$ , is a group homomorphism: indeed, since $T_{g}T_{h}=T_{hg}$ on $V$ , the dual action satisfies

$$ g\cdot(h\cdot w)=(hg)\cdot w. $$

If $g\cdot w=\chi(g)w$ and $h\cdot w=\chi(h)w$ , then

$$ (hg)\cdot w=g\cdot(h\cdot w)=g\cdot(\chi(h)w)=\chi(h)(g\cdot w)=\chi(h)\chi(g)w=\chi(g)\chi(h)w. $$

Thus $\chi$ is a character of $G$ . Conversely, if $\chi:G\to k^{\times}$ is a character and there exists a nonzero $w\in W$ with $g\cdot w=\chi(g)w$ for all $g\in G$ , then the line $k\cdot w$ is $G$ -stable. For each character $\chi:G\to k^{\times}$ , let $W_{\chi}\subseteq W$ be the subspace consisting of all $w\in W$ satisfying $g\cdot w=\chi(g)w$ for every $g\in G$ . From this identification, we obtain

$$ (\mathbb{P}(W))^{G}=\bigcup_{\begin{subarray}{c}\chi:G\to k^{\times}\\
W_{\chi}\neq 0\end{subarray}}\mathbb{P}(W_{\chi}). $$

Since $\iota$ is $G$ -equivariant,

$$ \iota(X^{G})=\iota(X)^{G}=\iota(X)\cap(\mathbb{P}(W))^{G}=\bigcup_{\chi}\big(\iota(X)\cap\mathbb{P}(W_{\chi})\big). $$

For projective $Y\subseteq\mathbb{P}(W)$ and linear $\Lambda\subseteq\mathbb{P}(W)$ one has $\deg(Y\cap\Lambda)\leq\deg(Y)$ . Recalling that there are at most $|G^{\mathrm{ab}}|$ characters $\chi:G\to k^{\times}$ , it follows that

$$ \displaystyle\deg_{M}(X^{G}) \displaystyle=\deg_{M}\Big(\bigcup_{\chi}\big(X\cap\mathbb{P}(W_{\chi})\big)\Big) \displaystyle\leq\sum_{\chi}\deg_{M}\big(X\cap\mathbb{P}(W_{\chi})\big) \displaystyle\leq\sum_{\chi}\deg_{M}(X) \displaystyle\leq|G^{\mathrm{ab}}|\deg_{M}(X). $$

Let $Z$ be an irreducible component of $X^{G}$ . For every $g\in G$ and every irreducible component $Z\subseteq X^{G}$ , we have

$$ (g^{*}L)|_{Z}=(g|_{Z})^{*}(L|_{g(Z)})=(\mathrm{id}_{Z})^{*}(L|_{Z})=L|_{Z}. $$

Hence

$$ c_{1}(M|_{Z})=\sum_{g\in G}c_{1}((g^{*}L)|_{Z})=|G|\cdot c_{1}(L|_{Z}). $$

Therefore

$$ \deg_{M}(Z)=|G|^{\mathrm{dim}(Z)}\deg_{L}(Z). $$

Summing over all components of $X^{G}$ gives

$$ \deg_{L}(X^{G})=\sum_{Z}\deg_{L}(Z)\leq\sum_{Z}|G|^{\dim Z}\deg_{L}(Z)=\deg_{M}(X^{G}). $$

Finally, set $D_{h}:=c_{1}(h^{*}L)$ . Then

$$ c_{1}(M)=\sum_{h\in G}D_{h},\qquad c_{1}(M)^{d}=\sum_{(h_{1},\dots,h_{d})\in G^{d}}D_{h_{1}}\cdots D_{h_{d}}. $$

By our assumption, the classes $D_{h}$ are all numerically equivalent to $c_{1}(L)$ . Hence every term in the expansion satisfies

$$ (D_{h_{1}}\cdots D_{h_{d}}\cdot[X])=(c_{1}(L)^{d}\cdot[X])=\deg_{L}(X). $$

As there are $|G|^{d}$ terms, we conclude that

$$ \deg_{M}(X)=(c_{1}(M)^{d}\cdot[X])=|G|^{d}\deg_{L}(X). $$

Combining (44), (46), and (47) shows that

$$ \deg_{L}(X^{G})\leq\deg_{M}(X^{G})\leq|G^{\mathrm{ab}}|\deg_{M}(X)=|G^{\mathrm{ab}}||G|^{d}\deg_{L}(X). $$

∎

As an immediate corollary, we obtain the following.

#### Corollary 7.4.

In the notation preceding Proposition 7.3, we have

$$ \deg_{\cal{L}_{s}}((\cal{A}_{s})^{\mu_{d}})\cdot 3^{\dim((\cal{A}_{s})^{\mu_{d}})}=\deg_{\cal{L}^{3}_{s}}((\cal{A}_{s})^{\mu_{d}})\leq\deg_{L^{3}}(A)d^{g+1}. $$

#### Proof.

We replace $L$ with $L^{3}$ so that $\cal{L}_{s}$ is very ample for $\cal{A}_{s}$ . Then the corollary follows immediately from Proposition 7.3 where we use the fact that $|G|=d$ and $\dim A=g$ . ∎

## 8. Uniform Bounds for Principally Polarized Abelian Varieties

We will now handle the general case of ppavs having at least one bad place of bad reduction which are not necessarily semistable. A naive approach would be to pass to the extension $K^{\prime}=\mathbb{C}(B^{\prime})=K(A[3])$ and apply (42). Although the degree $[K^{\prime}:K]$ is bounded in terms of $g$ , the issue is that $g(B^{\prime})$ can be arbitrarily large compared to $g(B)$ due to having no control a priori over the ramification.

By Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich, this problem can only happen when $A$ has many places of bad reduction over $K$ itself. If these places are of stable bad reduction, we may then pass to $K^{\prime}$ and apply Theorem 6.6. Hence the only remaining issue is if “most” of these places are in fact places of potentially good reduction, i.e., places which become good after passing to a semistable extension.

To handle this, we will show that every place $v$ of bad yet potentially good reduction contributes some uniform positive amount to our Arakelov-Green’s function $g_{n}$ . Then if there are many such places, we obtain a uniform positive lower bound on $g_{n}$ analogous to (38).

Let us first recall some definitions. Let $A/K$ be an abelian variety over a valued field $(K,|\cdot|)$ and let $L$ be a very ample line bundle on $A$ such that the embedding $\iota:A\xhookrightarrow{}\mathbb{P}^{N}$ by $L$ is projectively normal. Let $f:\mathbb{P}^{N}\to\mathbb{P}^{N}$ be an endomorphism over $K$ of degree $d$ that extends multiplication by $[m]$ for some $m\geq 2$ and let $F:\mathbb{A}^{N+1}\to\mathbb{A}^{N+1}$ be a homogeneous lift of $f$ . Given a basis $\cal{B}_{n}$ of $H^{0}(A,L^{n})$ , recall from §3 that we may define the Arakelov-Green’s function as

$$ g_{n}\left(P_{1},\dots,P_{c(n)}\right)=\frac{1}{c(n)}\sum_{i=1}^{c(n)}\widehat{H}_{F}(\widetilde{P_{i}})-\frac{1}{n\cdot c(n)}\log\left|\mathrm{det}\left(\eta_{j}(\widetilde{P_{i}})\right)_{\eta_{j}\in\mathcal{B}_{n}}\right|+r(F) $$

where $\widehat{H}_{F}$ is the local escape rate function, $\widetilde{P_{i}}$ are lifts of $P_{i}\in A(\overline{K}_{v})$ to $\mathbb{A}^{N+1}(\overline{K}_{v})$ . The correction $r(F)$ is a constant multiple of $\log|\operatorname{Res}(F)|$ to ensure that $g_{n}$ is independent of the choice of the lift $F$ . The quantity depends on the basis chosen $\cal{B}_{n}$ but any other basis will change the function by an additive constant.

In general, given a subset $T\subseteq A(\overline{K}_{v})$ where $\overline{K}_{v}$ is the completion of the algebraic closure of $K$ , we may define its (logarithmic) transfinite diameter with respect to $\cal{B}_{n}$ as

$$ \log d_{n,v}(\cal{B}_{n},T,L)=-\sup_{\vec{P}\in T^{c(n)}}g_{n,v}(P_{1},\ldots,P_{c(n)}), $$

where $\vec{P}=(P_{1},\dots,P_{c(n)})$ and we write $g_{n,v}$ for the Arakelov-Green’s function $g_{n}$ associated to $|\cdot|_{v}$ . Again, this depends on the choice of basis $\cal{B}_{n}$ ; however, the relative quantity

$$ \log d_{n,v}(T,L):=\log d_{n,v}(\cal{B}_{n},T,L)-\log d_{n,v}(\cal{B}_{n},A,L) $$

does not. If $K$ is a product formula field, then the global quantity

$$ \sum_{v\in M_{K}}\log d_{n,v}(\cal{B}_{n},A,L) $$

doesn’t depend on $\cal{B}_{n}$ and so it is useful to study this relative quantity $\log d_{n}(T,L)$ in order to obtain bounds on

$$ \sum_{v\in M_{K}}\log d_{n,v}(\cal{B}_{n},T,L). $$

We now state and prove the main result of this section.

#### Theorem 8.1.

Let $K$ be a non-archimedean discretely valued field with algebraically closed residue field $k$ . Let $A/K$ be a $g$ -dimensional ppav with principal polarization $\Theta$ and let $L$ be a line bundle representing $4\Theta$ . Assume that $A$ has bad reduction over $K$ but attains good reduction over a finite extension of $K$ . Let $T=A(K)$ . Then there are constants $N,\delta>0$ depending only on $g$ such that for all $n\geq N$ ,

$$ \log d_{n}(T,L)\leq\delta\log|\pi|. $$

where $\pi$ is a uniformizer of $K$ .

#### Proof.

The line bundle $L$ is very ample and its induced embedding $\iota:A\xhookrightarrow{}\mathbb{P}^{N}$ is projectively normal. Let $K^{\prime}=K(A[3])$ so that $A$ has good reduction over $K^{\prime}$ . Let $R$ and $R^{\prime}$ be the valuation rings. Then there is an abelian scheme $\cal{A}^{\prime}$ over $R^{\prime}$ whose generic fiber is $A$ . Let $\cal{N}/R$ be the Néron model for $A/K$ . Then $\cal{N}_{R^{\prime}}/R^{\prime}$ is a smooth model (but not the Néron model) for $A/K^{\prime}$ and by the Néron mapping property, we obtain an $R^{\prime}$ -morphism $f:\cal{N}_{R^{\prime}}\to\cal{A}^{\prime}$ . This gives us a morphism of special fibers $f_{s}:\cal{N}_{R^{\prime},s}\to\cal{A}^{\prime}_{s}$ and since our residue field is algebraically closed, we have $\cal{N}_{s}\simeq\cal{N}_{R^{\prime},s}$ and thus a morphism $f_{s}:\cal{N}_{s}\to\cal{A}^{\prime}_{s}$ .

The line bundle $L$ extends uniquely to a relatively ample line bundle $\cal{L}$ on $\cal{A}_{K^{\prime}}$ . By [88, Proposition 6.13], for each $n$ the $R^{\prime}$ -module $H^{0}(\cal{A}^{\prime},\cal{L}^{n})$ is free and hence has the same dimension as $H^{0}(A_{K^{\prime}},L^{n})$ and $H^{0}(\cal{A}^{\prime}_{s},\cal{L}_{s}^{n})$ . To compute $\log d_{n}(T,L)$ , we may choose any basis $\cal{B}_{n}$ we want: in particular, we choose $\cal{B}_{n}$ to be a basis of $H^{0}(\cal{A}^{\prime},\cal{L}^{n})$ . Then it is clear that $g_{\cal{B}_{n}}$ will be independent of the choice of such a basis, as the change of basis matrix between any two such bases satisfies $|\det|=1$ .

We first calculate $\log d_{n}(\cal{B}_{n},A,L).$

#### Lemma 8.2.

We have

$$ \log d_{n}(\cal{B}_{n},A,L)=0 $$

for all $n$ .

#### Proof.

Our line bundle $\cal{L}$ above gives us an embedding $\cal{A}^{\prime}\xhookrightarrow{}\mathbb{P}^{N}_{R^{\prime}}$ . By Proposition 6.5 and the fact that $R^{\prime}$ is a DVR, there exists an endomorphism $f:\mathbb{P}_{R^{\prime}}^{N}\to\mathbb{P}_{R^{\prime}}^{N}$ extending multiplication by $[m]$ on our abelian scheme $\cal{A}$ . Since $f$ is an endomorphism of $\mathbb{P}_{R^{\prime}}^{N}$ , we can pick a lift $F:\mathbb{A}_{K^{\prime}}^{N+1}\to\mathbb{A}_{K^{\prime}}^{N+1}$ such that $r(F)=0$ and the escape rate function on $\mathbb{A}^{N+1}$ is given by

$$ \widehat{H}_{F}((x_{0},\ldots,x_{N}))=\log\max\{|x_{0}|,\ldots,|x_{N}|\}. $$

Hence given $c(n)$ points $P_{1},\ldots,P_{c(n)}\in A(\overline{K})$ , picking affine lifts $\widetilde{P_{i}}=(x_{i,0},\ldots,x_{i,N})$ to $\mathbb{A}^{N+1}$ such that $\max_{0\leq j\leq N}\{|x_{i,j}|\}=1$ for all i, we obtain

$$ g_{n}(P_{1},\ldots,P_{c(n)})=-\frac{1}{n\cdot c(n)}\log\left|\mathrm{det}\left(\eta_{j}(\widetilde{P_{i}})\right)_{\eta_{j}\in\mathcal{B}_{n}}\right|. $$

Now each $\eta_{j}$ is a homogeneous polynomial with integral coefficients, and thus we clearly have $g_{n}(P_{1},\ldots,P_{c(n)})\geq 0$ and $\log d_{n}(\cal{B}_{n},A,L)\leq 0$ . On the other hand, as $\cal{B}_{n}$ is a basis of $H^{0}(\cal{A},\cal{L}^{n})$ , our determinant has absolute value $<1$ if and only if the reductions of $P_{i}$ to the special fiber $\cal{A}_{s}$ lie on $\operatorname{div}(t)$ for some nonzero $t\in H^{0}(\cal{A}_{s},\cal{L}_{s}^{n})$ . Clearly we may choose $P_{1},\ldots,P_{c(n)}\in A(\overline{K})$ such that this does not happen. We conclude that $\log d_{n}(\cal{B}_{n},A,L)=0$ .∎

We now bound $\log d_{n}(\cal{B}_{n},T,L)$ from above. By Proposition 7.1 and Corollary 7.4, we know that if $P_{i}\in A(K)$ , then their reductions in $\cal{A}_{s}$ lie on a subvariety $B$ with $\deg_{\cal{L}_{s}}(B)\leq D$ for some $D$ depending only on $g$ . Furthermore, this subvariety $B$ is a finite union of abelian subvarieties $B_{1},\ldots,B_{e}$ as noted in the discussion after Proposition 7.1. We may use the trivial upper bounds $e\leq D$ and $\deg_{\cal{L}_{s}}(B_{i})\leq D$ , to conclude that

$$ \dim H^{0}(B,\cal{L}_{s}^{n})\leq\sum_{i=1}^{e}\dim H^{0}(B_{i},\cal{L}_{s}^{n})\leq D^{2}n^{g-1} $$

where we are using the fact that for any abelian variety $C$ with an ample line bundle $L$ , we have

$$ \dim H^{0}(C,L^{n})=\frac{\deg_{L}(C)}{(\dim C)!}n^{\dim C}. $$

Since $\dim H^{0}(\cal{A}^{\prime}_{s},\cal{L}_{s}^{n})\geq\frac{n^{g}}{g!}$ , for some sufficiently large $n_{0}$ depending only on $g$ , we may find a nonzero section $\overline{s}$ of $H^{0}(\cal{A}^{\prime}_{s},\cal{L}_{s}^{n_{0}})$ that vanishes on $B$ . We may lift this to a section $s$ of $H^{0}(\cal{A}^{\prime},\cal{L}^{n_{0}})$ since $H^{0}(\cal{A}^{\prime},\cal{L}^{n_{0}})$ is free. For any $k,r\geq 1$ , consider the multiplication by $s^{k}$ map which sends $H^{0}(\cal{A}^{\prime},\cal{L}^{kn_{0}+r})$ to $H^{0}(\cal{A}^{\prime},\cal{L}^{2kn_{0}+r})$ . This map is injective on both the generic fiber and the special fiber. Since $H^{0}(\cal{A}^{\prime},\cal{L}^{2kn_{0}+r})$ is free, this means we may choose a basis of $H^{0}(\cal{A}^{\prime},\cal{L}^{2kn_{0}+r})$ such that $c(kn_{0})$ many of its elements are multiples of $s^{k}$ .

Given $n\geq 2n_{0}$ , we write $n$ in the form $2kn_{0}+r$ for $k\geq 1$ and $0\leq r<2n_{0}$ . We now compute $\log d_{n}(\cal{B}_{n},T,L)$ for $T\subseteq A(K)$ . Just as in Lemma 8.2, picking lifts $\tilde{P}_{i}$ with $\max\{|x_{i}|\}=1$ , we obtain

$$ g_{n}(P_{1},\ldots,P_{c(n)})=-\frac{1}{n\cdot c(n)}\log\left|\mathrm{det}\left(\eta_{j}(\widetilde{P_{i}})\right)_{\eta_{j}\in\mathcal{B}_{n}}\right|. $$

The reduction of each $\tilde{P}_{i}$ lies on the subvariety $B$ , and hence $|\eta(\tilde{P}_{i})|<1$ where $\eta$ is the homogeneous polynomial representing our section $s$ . As both $\eta_{j}$ and $\tilde{P}_{i}$ are defined over $K^{\prime}$ , we have

$$ |\eta(\tilde{P}_{i})|\leq|\pi|^{1/[K^{\prime}:K]}. $$

Now we have $c(\frac{n-r}{2})$ many $\eta_{j}$ ’s for which $\eta_{j}$ is an integral multiple of $\eta^{(n-r)/2n_{0}}$ . In particular,

$$ \log|\eta_{j}(\tilde{P}_{i})|\leq\frac{n-r}{2n_{0}[K^{\prime}:K]}\log|\pi|. $$

We have $c(\frac{n-r}{2})$ many such $\eta_{j}$ ’s and all other rows have $|\cdot|$ at most $1$ . Thus

$$ \frac{1}{n\cdot c(n)}\log\left|\mathrm{det}\left(\eta_{j}(\widetilde{P_{i}})\right)_{\eta_{j}\in\mathcal{B}_{n}}\right|\leq\frac{c(\frac{n-r}{2})(n-r)}{2n_{0}[K^{\prime}:K]nc(n)}\log|\pi|\leq\delta\log|\pi| $$

for some $\delta>0$ depending only on $g$ as desired. ∎

We can now extend Corollary 6.7 to the non-semistable case. Recall that we say a place $v\in M_{K}$ has stable bad reduction if $A/K_{v}$ does not have potential good reduction.

#### Corollary 8.3.

Let $g\geq 1$ and let $K=\mathbb{C}(B)$ be the function field of a smooth projective curve $B/\mathbb{C}$ . Let $g(B)$ be the genus of $B$ . There are positive integers $M_{0}=M_{0}(g,g(B))$ and $n=n(g,g(B))$ and an $\epsilon=\epsilon(g,g(B))>0$ with the following property. Let $(A,\Theta)$ be a dimension $g$ principally polarized abelian variety over $K$ . Let $L=4\Theta$ , and let $S_{0}$ be the set of places of stably bad reduction for $A$ and let $S$ be the set of all places of bad reduction. Assume that $|S|\geq 1$ . Then either:

- • $|S_{0}|\geq\max\left\{1,\dfrac{h_{\omega}(A)}{M_{0}}\right\}$ , or

- • for any $T\subseteq A(K)$ , either $T$ is contained in $\operatorname{div}(s)$ for some $s\in H^{0}(A,\mathcal{L}^{n})$ , or

$$ \frac{1}{|T|}\sum_{x\in T}\widehat{h}_{A,L}(x)\geq\varepsilon h_{\omega}(A). $$

#### Proof.

Let $S$ be the places of bad reduction of $A/K$ and let $S_{0}^{\prime}$ denote the set of places of unstable bad reduction of $A$ , i.e., those places of bad reduction which become places of good reduction upon passage to a semistable extension. Then $S=S_{0}\sqcup S_{0}^{\prime}$ . Let $K^{\prime}=K(A[3])$ and let $g(B^{\prime})$ be the genus of $B^{\prime}$ where $K^{\prime}=\mathbb{C}(B^{\prime})$ . By (42), there are positive constants $C_{1}$ and $C_{2}$ depending only on $g$ such that

$$ h_{\omega}(A)\leq C_{1}|S_{0}|+C_{2}\max\{g(B^{\prime}),1\}. $$

Now observe that $K^{\prime}/K$ can only be ramified over places in $S$ and thus

$$ g(B^{\prime})\leq[K^{\prime}:K](|S|+g(B)). $$

Hence for some $C_{3}>0$ depending only on $g$ , we have

$$ h_{\omega}(A)\leq C_{1}|S_{0}|+C_{3}(|S|+g(B)+1). $$

It follows that if $M_{0}\gg_{g,g(B)}1$ and $|S_{0}|<\max\{1,\frac{h_{\omega}(A)}{M_{0}}\}$ , then

$$ |S^{\prime}_{0}|\geq\frac{h_{\omega}(A)}{M_{0}}, $$

as we have assumed that $|S|\geq 1$ . Now for any basis $\cal{B}_{n}$ of $H^{0}(A,L^{n})$ , Theorem 3.1 implies (similarly as in (20)) that

$$ \sum_{v\in M_{K}}\log d_{n}(\cal{B}_{n},A,L)\leq C\frac{\log n}{n}h_{\omega}(A) $$

for some $C>0$ depending only on $g$ . For each $v\in S^{\prime}_{0}$ , Theorem 8.1 tells us that

$$ \log d_{n}(\cal{B}_{n},T,L)-\log d_{n}(\cal{B}_{n},A,L)\leq\delta\log|\pi|=-\delta $$

as $\log|\pi|=-1$ . Hence we get

$$ \sum_{v\in M_{K}}\log d_{n}(\cal{B}_{n},T,L)\leq C\frac{\log n}{n}h_{\omega}(A)-\delta\frac{h_{\omega}(A)}{M_{0}}\leq-\frac{\delta}{2M_{0}}h_{\omega}(A) $$

when $n\gg_{g,g(B)}1$ . Since for any set of $c(n)$ points $x_{1},\dots,x_{c(n)}\in T$ which do not all lie in $\operatorname{div}(s)$ for any nonzero section $s\in H^{0}(A,L^{n})$ , we have

$$ \frac{1}{c(n)}\sum_{i=1}^{c(n)}\widehat{h}_{A,L}(x_{i})=\sum_{v\in M_{K}}g_{\cal{B}_{n},v}(x_{1},\ldots,x_{c(n)})\geq\sum_{v\in M_{K}}-\log d_{n}(\cal{B}_{n},T,L), $$

it follows that either

$$ \frac{1}{c(n)}\sum_{i=1}^{c(n)}\widehat{h}_{A,L}(x_{i})\geq\frac{\delta}{2M_{0}}h_{\omega}(A), $$

or there exists a nonzero $s\in H^{0}(A,L^{n})$ such that any set of $c(n)$ elements of $T$ is contained in $\operatorname{div}(s)$ . As seen in the proof of Theorem 6.6, the latter implies that there exists a nonzero $s\in H^{0}(A,L^{n})$ such that all elements of $T$ lie in $\operatorname{div}(s)$ . This completes the proof of the Corollary.∎

Combining Corollary 8.3 with Theorem 6.6, we obtain the following. For a ppav $(A,\Theta)$ , let $L=4\Theta$ and let $\widehat{h}_{A,L}$ denote the Néron–Tate height with respect to $L$ .

#### Theorem 8.4.

Let $K=\mathbb{C}(B)$ be the function field of a smooth projective curve $B$ over $\mathbb{C}$ and let $g(B)$ be the genus of $B$ . Let $g\geq 1$ be a positive integer. Then there is a positive integer $n=n(g,g(B))$ and a positive constant $\varepsilon=\varepsilon(g,g(B))>0$ such that for any $g$ -dimensional ppav $(A,\Theta)$ with at least one place of bad reduction, the set

$$ \{x\in A(K)\mid\widehat{h}_{A,L}(x)\leq\varepsilon h_{\omega}(A)\} $$

is contained in $\operatorname{div}(s)$ for some $s\in H^{0}(A,L^{n})$ .

## 9. The case of Everywhere Good Reduction

We now handle the case where we have a principally polarized abelian variety $A$ of dimension $g$ with everywhere good reduction. By (42), such abelian varieties must have Faltings height bounded uniformly from above and so it suffices to handle this setting. We will prove the following theorem. For a ppav $(A,\lambda)$ , let $L$ be a symmetric ample line bundle inducing $\lambda$ and let $\widehat{h}_{A}$ denote the Néron–Tate height induced by $L$ .

#### Theorem 9.1.

Let $K=\mathbb{C}(B)$ for a smooth projective curve $B$ over $\mathbb{C}$ and let $M,\delta>0$ . Then there exists a natural number $N\geq 1$ , depending only on $(g,g(B),M,\delta)$ , such that for any principally polarized semistable abelian variety $A/K$ of dimension $g$ and $h_{\omega}(A)\leq M$ , the set

$$ \left\{x\in A(K)/\operatorname{Tr}_{K/\mathbb{C}}(A)(\mathbb{C})\mid\widehat{h}_{A}(x)\leq\delta\right\}\leq N. $$

Since $\widehat{h}_{A}(y)=0$ for $y\in\operatorname{Tr}_{K/\mathbb{C}}(A)(\mathbb{C})$ , the quantity $\widehat{h}_{A}(x)$ is independent of the choice of representative for $x\in A(K)/\operatorname{Tr}_{K/\mathbb{C}}(A)(\mathbb{C})$ and hence well-defined. When $\operatorname{Tr}_{K/\mathbb{C}}(A)=0$ is trivial, this gives an upper bound on the number of small points of $A(K)$ .

For a number field $K$ , the analogous statement of Theorem 9.1 is relatively straightforward. Using the work of David–Philippon [28], we may find an embedding $A\xhookrightarrow{}\mathbb{P}^{N}$ such that any $x\in A(K)$ with $\widehat{h}_{A}(x)\leq\delta$ has Weil height at most $\delta^{\prime}$ , with $\delta^{\prime}$ depending only on $(g,M,\delta)$ . It then follows from the Northcott property that there is a uniform bound on the number of such points.

For a function field $K=\mathbb{C}(B)$ , however, the Northcott property does not hold and we have to obtain finiteness through other means. Our strategy is to follow the proof of the Lang–Néron theorem [26], which is the analogue of Mordell–Weil for function fields. This uses the number of irreducible components of a $\operatorname{Hom}$ scheme, with an upper bound on the degree, as a replacement for the Northcott property. We will then relate the components of a $\operatorname{Hom}$ scheme to that of a Hilbert scheme, where we can use the theory of Gotzmann numbers to obtain uniform upper bounds. Our proof can be broken into three parts:

- (i) Construct a variety $\tilde{A}\subseteq\mathbb{P}^{N}_{B}=\mathbb{P}^{N}\times_{\mathbb{C}}B$ whose generic fiber is isomorphic to $A/K$ which is cut out by equations with degree bounded only in terms of $g,g(B),M,\delta$ . Observe that $\mathbb{P}^{N}\times_{\mathbb{C}}B=\mathbb{P}^{N}\times B$ as we are working with varieties over $\mathbb{C}$ .

- (ii) Reduce Theorem 9.1 to a problem on bounding the number of irreducible components of the Hilbert scheme of $\tilde{A}$ , with the coefficients of the Hilbert polynomial bounded only in terms of $g,g(B),M,\delta$ .

- (iii) Apply the work of Gotzmann [70, Section 5] to obtain uniform bounds on the number of irreducible components depending only on $g,g(B),M,\delta$ .

We first show that we may assume the existence of a level $3$ structure for $A$ over $K$ .

#### Proposition 9.2.

Let $A/K$ be a semistable abelian variety of dimension $g$ and assume that $h_{\omega}(A)\leq M$ . Let $K^{\prime}=K(A[3])$ , so that $A/K^{\prime}$ has level $3$ structure. Let $K^{\prime}=\mathbb{C}(B^{\prime})$ and $K=\mathbb{C}(B)$ . Then $g(B^{\prime})$ can be bounded purely in terms of $(g,g(B),M)$ .

#### Proof.

By Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich, the extension $K^{\prime}/K$ can only be ramified over places of bad reduction for $A/K$ . Now if $S$ denotes the number of places of bad reduction, then for $p=3$ , we have $h_{\partial\cal{A}_{g,3}}(A)\geq|S|$ since $\lambda_{v,\partial\cal{A}_{g,3}}(A)\geq 1$ for each place $v$ of bad reduction for $A/K$ . As there exists a constant $c=c(g)>0$ for which

$$ M\geq h_{\omega}(A)>ch_{\partial\cal{A}_{g,3}}(A), $$

it follows that $|S|$ is bounded in terms of $g$ and $M$ . Hence the degree of the ramification divisor for $\pi:B^{\prime}\to B$ is bounded by $|S|[K^{\prime}:K]$ , which is bounded in terms of $g$ and $M$ . As the degree of $\pi$ is bounded in terms of $g$ , by Riemann–Hurwitz, we thus have that $g(B^{\prime})$ is bounded in terms of $(g,g(B),M)$ as desired. ∎

By Proposition 9.2, we may now replace $K$ with $K(A[3])$ for Theorem 9.1 and $g(B^{\prime})$ remains bounded in terms of the initial data $(g,g(B),M)$ . The constants $M,\delta$ can be replaced by $[K^{\prime}:K]M$ and $[K^{\prime}:K]\delta$ which is bounded in terms of $(g,M,\delta)$ . By the proof of [26, Lemma 7.3], we have an injection

$$ A(K)/\operatorname{Tr}_{K/\mathbb{C}}(A)(\mathbb{C})\xhookrightarrow{}A(K^{\prime})/\operatorname{Tr}_{K^{\prime}/\mathbb{C}}(A)(\mathbb{C}) $$

and hence we may assume without loss that $A$ has level $3$ structure defined over $K$ .

Recall from Proposition 6.4 that we have open sets $U_{1},\ldots,U_{m}$ covering $\mathcal{A}_{g,3}$ such that on each $U_{i}$ , we have an embedding $\mathcal{A}_{U_{i}}\hookrightarrow\mathbb{P}^{N_{i}}_{U_{i}}$ and a morphism $F:\mathbb{P}^{N_{i}}_{U_{i}}\to\mathbb{P}^{N_{i}}_{U_{i}}$ of degree $n_{i}^{2}$ that extends multiplication-by- $[n_{i}]$ . Moreover, the $n_{i}$ and $N_{i}$ may be chosen to depend only on $g$ . Without loss of generality, let $A/K$ with its level $3$ structure define a point on $U_{1}(K)$ . We let $F_{A}$ be the corresponding morphism on $\mathbb{P}_{K}^{N_{1}}$ induced by our point on $U_{1}(K)$ . Let $F$ be given by $[F_{0}:\cdots:F_{N_{1}}]$ . We define

$$ h(F):=\sum_{v\in M_{K}}\log\max\{|F_{0}|_{v},\ldots,|F_{N_{1}}|_{v}\} $$

where $|F_{i}|_{v}$ is the maximum of the absolute values of the coefficients of $F_{i}$ .

#### Proposition 9.3.

There exists a $c_{1}>0$ depending only on $g$ such that

$$ h(F_{A})\leq c_{1}h_{\omega}(A). $$

#### Proof.

We apply Proposition 2.9 with $X=U_{1},Y=\mathrm{Mor}_{n_{1}^{2}}(\mathbb{P}^{N_{1}},\mathbb{P}^{N_{1}})$ , $\varphi$ sending $[B]\in U_{1}(K)$ to the corresponding $F_{B}\in Y$ , $L=\omega$ on $\mathcal{A}_{g,p}^{*}$ , and $M=\mathcal{O}(1)$ on the compactification of $Y$ that yields the Weil height $h(F)$ . This gives us our constant $c_{1}>0$ such that

$$ h(F_{A})\leq c_{1}h_{\omega}(A) $$

, as desired.∎

Let $\mathcal{P}_{1},\ldots,\mathcal{P}_{m}$ be homogeneous polynomials of degree $t$ on $\mathbb{P}^{N_{1}}_{U_{1}}$ that cut out $\mathcal{A}_{U_{1}}$ . Pulling back along the $K$ -point $[A]$ gives equations $P_{1},\ldots,P_{m}$ of degree $t$ that cut out $A$ inside $\mathbb{P}^{N_{1}}_{K}$ . Let $h(P_{i})$ denote the maximum height of its coefficients.

#### Proposition 9.4.

There exists a $c_{2}>0$ depending only on $g$ such that $h(P_{i})\leq c_{2}\,h_{\omega}(A)$ for all $i$ .

#### Proof.

Let $a$ be a coefficient of some $P_{i}$ . It suffices to prove the existence of $c>0$ depending only on $g$ such that $h(a)\leq c\,h_{\omega}(A)$ . Let $\mathfrak{a}$ be the function on $U_{1}$ that represents the coefficient $a$ . Then $\mathfrak{a}:U_{1}\to\mathbb{A}^{1}$ is a morphism over $\mathbb{C}$ . Applying Proposition 2.9 with $X=U_{1}$ , $Y=\mathbb{A}^{1}$ (compactified to $\mathbb{P}^{1}$ ), $\varphi=\mathfrak{a}$ , $L=\omega$ on $\cal{A}_{g,3}^{*}$ , and $M=\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{1}}(1)$ , we obtain $h(a)\leq c\,h_{\omega}(A)$ as desired. ∎

We now proceed with the first step, which is to construct a closed subvariety $\tilde{A}\subseteq\mathbb{P}^{N_{1}}_{B}=\mathbb{P}_{\mathbb{C}}^{N_{1}}\times B$ whose generic fiber is $A$ embedded in $\mathbb{P}^{N_{1}}_{K}$ . Furthermore, we would like to control the degree of equations that cut out $\tilde{A}$ with respect to some ample line bundle on $\mathbb{P}_{B}^{N_{1}}$ .

We first pick a base point $z_{0}\in B(\mathbb{C})$ . We have equations $F_{i}(x_{0},\ldots,x_{N_{1}})$ of degree $\leq t$ and height $\leq c_{2}M$ that cut out $A$ inside $\mathbb{P}^{N_{1}}_{K}$ . We may assume that $c_{2}M$ is a positive integer. By scaling, we may further assume that there is one coefficient of $F_{i}$ which is $1$ . Then for any other coefficient $a$ of $F_{i}$ , we have $h(a)\leq c_{2}M$ . Viewing $a$ as a function of $B$ , this means that the number of poles $a$ has on $B$ is at most $c_{2}M$ .

#### Proposition 9.5.

There exists an integer $M^{\prime}>0$ , depending only on $(g,g(B),M)$ , and $f_{A}\in K^{\times}$ with $\operatorname{div}(f_{A})\geq-M^{\prime}[z_{0}]$ , depending on $A$ , such that for every $i$ , the coefficients of the polynomial $f_{A}F_{i}$ are functions on $B$ with poles only on $z_{0}$ . In particular, $\operatorname{div}(f_{A}a)\geq-(M^{\prime}+c_{2}M)[z_{0}]$ for each coefficient $a$ of $F_{i}$ .

#### Proof.

Let $a$ be a coefficient of some $F_{i}$ . Then as $a$ has at most $M$ poles on $B$ , by Riemann–Roch we may find a function $f_{A}\in K^{\times}$ (depending on $A$ ) with $\operatorname{div}(f_{A})\geq-(c_{2}M+g(B)+1)[z_{0}]$ such that $f_{a}a$ only has poles at $z_{0}$ . Doing this for each coefficient and multiplying the various $f_{A}$ ’s together gives us a $f_{A}$ such that $f_{A}a$ only has poles at $z_{0}$ for any coefficient $a$ of any $F_{i}$ . As the number of coefficients is bounded in terms of $g$ , it follows that the order of the pole of $f_{A}$ at $z_{0}$ is bounded in terms of $(g,g(B),M)$ as desired. ∎

Let $f=f_{A}$ be the function in Proposition 9.5. Then the coefficients of $fF_{i}$ all have poles only on $z_{0}$ with order at most $M^{\prime}+c_{2}M$ . Let

$$ L=\mathcal{O}_{B}\big((M^{\prime}+c_{2}M)z_{0}\big). $$

Then as each coefficient $a_{\alpha}$ of $F_{i}$ satisfies $\mathrm{div}(fa_{\alpha})\geq-(M^{\prime}+c_{2}M)[z_{0}]$ , we may view $fa_{\alpha}$ as an element of $H^{0}(B,L)$ . We now construct our subvariety $\tilde{A}$ of $\mathbb{P}_{B}^{N_{1}}$ .

#### Proposition 9.6.

There exists a constant $C_{1}>0$ , depending only on $(g,g(B),M)$ such that the following holds: there is an embedding $\mathbb{P}_{\mathbb{C}}^{N_{1}}\times B\xhookrightarrow{}\mathbb{P}^{N}$ along with a closed subvariety $\tilde{A}\subseteq\mathbb{P}_{\mathbb{C}}^{N_{1}}\times B$ , whose generic fiber is $A/K$ , such that $\tilde{A}$ is cut out by equations of degree at most $C_{1}$ .

#### Proof.

Let $p_{1}:\mathbb{P}^{N_{1}}\times B\to\mathbb{P}^{N_{1}}$ and $p_{2}:\mathbb{P}^{N_{1}}\times B\to B$ be the coordinate projections. Viewing $F_{i}$ as a homogeneous degree- $t$ polynomial in $X_{0},\dots,X_{N_{1}}$ , each monomial $X^{\alpha}$ with $|\alpha|=t$ is a section of $\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{N_{1}}}(t)$ , and hence pulls back to a section of $p_{1}^{*}\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{N_{1}}}(t)$ on $\mathbb{P}^{N_{1}}\times B$ . Each coefficient $fa_{\alpha}$ is a section of $L$ on $B$ , hence pulls back to a section of $p_{2}^{*}L$ on $\mathbb{P}^{N_{1}}\times B$ . The resulting products $fa_{\alpha}F_{i}$ give sections of $p_{1}^{*}\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{N_{1}}}(t)\otimes p_{2}^{*}L$ , and summing over all monomials $X^{\alpha}$ with $|\alpha|=t$ shows that $fF_{i}$ is a global section of this line bundle.

Choose $M^{\prime}>0$ such that $\deg L=M^{\prime}+c_{2}M>2g(B)+1$ . (Recall that $c_{2}M\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0}$ .) Then $|L|$ embeds $B$ into $\mathbb{P}^{m}$ with $L\simeq\varphi_{L}^{*}\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{m}}(1)$ . Under this embedding, $p_{2}^{*}L\simeq\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{N_{1}}\times\mathbb{P}^{m}}(0,1)$ and hence

$$ p_{1}^{*}\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{N_{1}}}(t)\otimes p_{2}^{*}L\simeq\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{N_{1}}\times\mathbb{P}^{m}}(t,1). $$

Thus each $fF_{i}$ is bihomogeneous of bidegree $(t,1)$ on $\mathbb{P}^{N_{1}}\times\mathbb{P}^{m}$ . The sections $\{fF_{1},\dots,fF_{m}\}$ define a common zero locus $\tilde{A}\subseteq\mathbb{P}^{N_{1}}\times B$ . Let $\eta=\operatorname{Spec}\,\mathbb{C}(B)$ be the generic point of $B$ . Base-changing $\mathbb{P}^{N_{1}}\times B$ along $\eta\hookrightarrow B$ gives
